## 2026-06-12 — E2E Chrome-driven walkthrough + redundancy audit — DONE

- **What:** Drove the dev SPA (`npm run dev` on :3000) through all 18 sidebar routes via Chrome DevTools MCP, logged in as Owner (`tonywei.office@gmail.com` + email OTP), captured screenshots for each screen into `tmp/e2e-screens/`, probed the recent pure-jasa Rakit flow as the deep-dive target (per latest commit `67ff9ae`).
- **Verdict:** mostly **PASS** on golden paths, but found **1 confirmed UX bug**, several **data-quality / cosmetic bugs**, and **clear redundancy clusters** worth a cleanup pass before Phase 1.

### Confirmed bug — Penjualan Baru Rakit line is invisible in cart
- Reproduction: Catat Penjualan → `+ Tambah Jasa Rakit` → fill description ("E2E TEST — Box Test Probe") + Estimasi Harga 500 000 + HPP 300 000 → `+ Tambah ke Cart`.
- Observed: cart subtotal jumps to `Rp 500.000` AND `Subtotal barang Rp 500.000` / `Total Invoice Rp 500.000` AND the green "💡 Cart pure-jasa — invoice langsung dicetak tanpa lock/approval." banner appears AND submit button correctly reads "💾 Simpan & Cetak Invoice Lunas" (so the recent commit's data routing is correct), BUT the cart counter still reads `0 ITEM` and the empty-state text `"Belum ada item. Tambahkan dari hasil pencarian di atas."` stays. The added rakit description appears NOWHERE on the page (`document.body.innerText.includes('E2E TEST') === false`).
- Impact: user fills the form, clicks add, sees no row, may add it again — easy way to silently double-invoice. The pure-jasa Lunas routing fix is shipping on top of a cart-render bug that predates it.
- Screenshot: `tmp/e2e-screens/09-rakit-ghost-line.png`.

### Other bugs / friction observed
- **Stok Opname history** — sessions #170/#171 show counter/witness as raw `00000000` instead of resolved user names. (Looks like a join failure or seeded test sessions with placeholder UUIDs leaking to UI.)
- **User Management** — Eva renders "21/13 aktif" permissions. 21 > 13 is impossible math; suggests the count of *active* keys diverges from the count of *known* keys after the permission catalog grew. Re-normalize.
- **Material Icons not rendering** on Notification Settings + User Management + multiple screens — buttons show ligature names as literal text: `magic_button BUAT AKUN`, `monitor_heart`, `inventory_2`, `timer`. Font is either missing for these pages or the surrounding span misses the `material-icons` class.
- **Pengaturan / Profil Perusahaan** — `Nama Perusahaan: TEST_DO_NOT_SAVE` (test bleed into the production company-name field; this string ends up on every invoice).
- **Notification Settings / Pengaturan WA recipients** — many T20 stress-test rows with 21-digit phone numbers (`628116473880667475576`, etc.). Invalid IDs polluting the canonical recipient list.
- **Pelanggan + Pipeline** — WhatsApp leads display as raw JIDs (`154671050153994@lid`, `6282114341213@s.whatsapp.net`). No auto-resolve to a customer name; the Customer 360 promise breaks for AI-originated leads.
- **Sales Inbox** — multiple `ESCALATED: Gemini failed after 10 retries` rows on the visible page. Production Gemini calls are intermittently failing all retries; surfaces as user-facing "Mohon maaf, sistem kami sedang sibuk." Worth checking quota / region.
- **WhatsApp AI screen** — "Daemon online" pill renders even when daemon is offline (we never started `backend-go`); below it the actual state correctly says "Menunggu QR dari daemon...". Pill should reflect ping result, not be hardcoded.
- **Dashboard / Laporan** — top products are mostly test data ("Test", "Test Item", "Test SKU", "Line B"); the only real-looking row is "Jasa Rakit — Box Wiring PT XYZ". Production-shaped reports will only become meaningful after a test-data purge.
- **Recharts** warns about `width(-1) height(-1)` on first paint of Dashboard charts — cosmetic but consistently logged.
- **Console** — small `Failed to load resource: 404` + an "empty `src` attribute" warning on every page (probably a missing icon/logo asset).

### Redundancy findings (per the 4 categories you picked)

**A. Duplicate UI surfaces**
1. **Three entry points → same screen**: sidebar "Notification Settings · Detak Jantung WA" AND top-nav "Settings" AND top-nav "Konfigurasi Histori" all open the same Notification-heartbeat config screen. The two top-nav buttons add zero functionality.
2. **Kasir → "📋 Catat Penjualan"** big CTA duplicates the sidebar "Catat Penjualan" entry. Quick-action is fine in principle, but the button is given premium real-estate while doing exactly what the always-visible sidebar already does.
3. **Stock Manager → "Stok Opname"** button shortcuts to the same screen as the sidebar "Stok Opname" entry. Same critique.
4. **Dashboard → "Buka Inbox Chat"** CTA duplicates sidebar "Sales Inbox".
5. Sidebar uses the word "Rekonsiliasi" for two unrelated things — "**Kasir** · Rekonsiliasi Harian" (daily kasir close) and "**Rekonsiliasi** · Tutup Buku Bulanan" (monthly bank recon). Not technically duplicated, but the shared word causes confusion when scanning the menu.

**B. Overlapping data models / fields**
1. **WA recipients list is editable from TWO places**: `Notification Settings` AND `Pengaturan`. Same rows render in both; unclear which is canonical. Pick one, link from the other.
2. **Bank account** is configured in BOTH `Pengaturan → Rekening Bank` (legacy single-row: BCA / 5271166282 / Tony) AND in `Rekonsiliasi → Rekening Aktif` (multi-row, currently `BCA Bisnis`). The build snapshot §13.4 already labels this "legacy single-row" — the legacy surface should be deleted from `Pengaturan` so users don't edit the wrong record.
3. **Dual-warehouse `stock_atas` / `stock_bawah`** is effectively unused. Of ~50 rows visible in Stock Manager, all but a handful have `Bawah: 0`. The dual-warehouse model is shipped throughout the schema (transfer RPC, FIFO, ledger sources, UI columns) but operationally everything sits in "atas". Either commit and seed bawah, or collapse to a single `stock` field plus a future N-warehouse model.
4. **WhatsApp JID ↔ customer** — `customers` rows carry `+62...` phone numbers but Pipeline / Pelanggan / Sales Inbox show JIDs (`@lid`, `@s.whatsapp.net`) for AI-originated leads. The data is effectively two siloed identities for the same human; needs a join.
5. **HPP shown twice on a sale** — Kasir tx rows show `HPP Rp 800.000` AND the Laporan KPI shows `HPP (Harga Modal)` derived from the same field. Acceptable, but worth checking whether the per-line HPP and the rolled-up HPP can diverge after a Rakit material-edit reversal (out of scope for this sweep).

**C. Dead / misleading navigation**
1. **"Konfigurasi Histori"** — name suggests *configuration audit history*, which would actually be useful (build snapshot §13.4 explicitly says "Audit log UI 🟡 Tables exist — no unified UI"). The button instead routes to Notification Settings. Either rename it ("Notifikasi") or repurpose it to a real config-history view backed by `reconciliation_audit_log`, `rakit_audit_log`, `approval_requests`.
2. **"Settings"** in top-nav adds nothing beyond duplicating Notification Settings — and is in English while every other label is Indonesian. Delete.
3. **Pipeline** screen brands itself as a sales kanban but renders a flat list filtered by status pill (Semua/Aktif/Eskalasi/Selesai/Gugur). The build snapshot §7.4 already acknowledges "Drag-drop status transitions 🟡 View-only currently" — but then the value-add over Order History is unclear; consider folding Pipeline into Order History with a "Tahap Pipeline" filter.
4. **WhatsApp AI** screen has no useful local affordance when the daemon isn't running; for an Owner who never touches the daemon, this nav item is permanent dead weight. Consider hiding behind a permission or under Pengaturan.

**D. Workflow steps that feel pointless**
1. **Rakit form** has a "+ Tambah ke Cart" sub-button inside the sub-form even though the parent cart has its own "Simpan & Cetak Invoice" submit. With the ghost-line bug above, the intermediate Add step costs the user a click and gives no visual feedback — collapse the sub-form's submit straight into "Simpan & Cetak Invoice" if the form is valid.
2. **PO list** is dominated by `PO-TEST-1780915984037581000` rows with `Rp 0` totals, all marked "Terlambat". Whatever process is creating these should not surface them in the operator's overdue queue.
3. **Top bar** carries: search box "Cari menu…" + notification bell + system info button + Settings + Konfigurasi Histori — five widgets to maintain a screen that mostly just routes between sidebar items. The sidebar itself has 18 entries. Either commit to a top bar with real verbs (global search, profile) or remove it.
4. **Sidebar count is 18** — even with no Phase 1 additions this is more than the cognitive limit for first-time users. Likely groupings: Sales (Kasir, Catat Penjualan, Riwayat Pesanan, Pipeline, Pelanggan, Sales Inbox), Inventory (Stock Manager, Stok Opname, WIP Rakit), Finance (Pembelian, Rekonsiliasi, Persetujuan), Insights (Dashboard, Laporan), System (User Mgmt, Notifications, WhatsApp AI, Pengaturan). Five sections × 3-6 items is friendlier than a flat 18.

- **Problem**: Cart with only Jasa Rakit / Jasa Custom Panel (no SKU items) couldn't reach "Simpan & Cetak Invoice Lunas" — `handleSave` validation toasted "Tambahkan minimal 1 item" because it only checked `cart.length === 0`, and even past that gate, `if (hasRakit)` forced every cart with jasa lines through WIP + lock-approval.
- **Change**:
  - **RPC migration** `supabase/migrations/20260610000001_record_kasir_sale_service_lines.sql` (`c628dde`, fix `2fcaf53`): `record_kasir_sale` skips items where `sku IS NULL` in the (sku, warehouse) aggregation loop — no `decrement_stock`, no `deduct_stock_fifo`. The per-item re-emit loop branches on `v_sku IS NULL` and passes `hpp_per_unit` / `hpp_subtotal` from the input verbatim (`COALESCE(..., 0)` for missing fields; service-line `v_qty` defaults to 1 to prevent NULL-poisoning `v_hpp_total`). Service-line HPP still adds to `v_hpp_total` so `kasir_transactions.hpp_total` matches cart cost. Carried forward `p_payment_subtype` / `p_dp_input_type` validation from migration `20260609000003`. Applied to live Supabase via psql.
  - **`RakitInlineForm`** (`3f5f40e`, breakpoint fix `cdaa355`): added "HPP (modal)" number input alongside "Estimasi Harga" in a `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2` layout. `onAdd` callback payload widens to `{type, description, estimatedPrice, hppEstimate}`.
  - **`PenjualanBaruScreen`** (`67ff9ae`): `rakitLines` state shape gains `hppEstimate`. New derived gates `isMixedCart = hasRakit && cart.length > 0` and `isPureJasa = hasRakit && cart.length === 0`. Validation accepts pure-jasa cart (`'Tambahkan minimal 1 item atau jasa.'`). The WIP branch trigger is now `if (isMixedCart)` so pure-jasa falls through to the existing `recordSale` path with `items: [...skuItems, ...serviceItems]` where service items carry `sku: null, qty: 1, unit_price/hpp_per_unit` from the cart. New emerald "💡 Cart pure-jasa" banner; the amber WIP banner copy is updated to "karena ada SKU + jasa rakit di cart yang sama".
  - **`KasirItem` type** (`67ff9ae`): `sku: string | null` and `warehouse: WarehouseLocation | null`. Existing JSX consumers (`KasirInvoiceModal`, `OrderHistoryScreen`, `SalesInvoicePDF`) render null as nothing so no string-op consumer was broken.
  - **`salesEntries.ts`** (`ada2d0a`): coerce `KasirItem.sku ?? undefined` at the `SalesEntry.items.sku` boundary so `null` doesn't leak into a `string | undefined` contract.
  - **`SalesInvoicePDF`** (`ae06fb3`): render the `<div>{item.sku}</div>` subtitle only when `item.sku` is truthy, so service lines don't show an empty subtitle row.
- **Tests**: 2 new integration tests in `tests/integration/sales-recording.test.ts` pin the null-sku RPC happy-path (stock untouched, HPP propagates verbatim) and the mixed-cart RPC contract (SKU line deducts stock by 1, service line passes HPP through, `hpp_total = FIFO + verbatim`). All 4 tests in `describe('record_kasir_sale RPC')` pass against live Supabase. `npm run lint`: 0 errors. `vite build` clean → bundle `index-BdOgndk0.js`.
- **Verified live (Cloud Run revision shipping `index-BdOgndk0.js`)**:
  - Pure-jasa Lunas: jasa rakit only (Rp 1.5jt / HPP 800k) → invoice `WLK-20260612-016` prints with the service description, no SKU subtitle, no WIP detour. Dashboard OMSET reflects +Rp 1.5jt, PESANAN TERPROSES +1, no Persetujuan badge.
  - Mixed cart regression: SKU "Box Panel — Ukuran Kecil" + jasa rakit → amber WIP banner shows "SKU + jasa rakit di cart yang sama", save routes to WIP list with status `WIP`, transaction visible for lock submission. No regression on the existing flow.
  - Empty cart toast: clicking Simpan with empty cart + no jasa lines → toast `"Tambahkan minimal 1 item atau jasa."` exactly.
  - Console clean across all three scenarios.

## 2026-06-10 — Bug fix: Persetujuan inbox blank — DONE

- **Root cause**: `subscribeApprovalRequests` in `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts` used a hard-coded channel topic `approval_requests_inbox`. Sidebar.tsx already subscribes to that topic on app mount for the badge count; when the user opens the Persetujuan inbox, `ApprovalInboxScreen` calls the same helper, supabase-js reuses the existing channel by topic name, and `.on('postgres_changes', ...)` after `.subscribe()` throws `cannot add postgres_changes callbacks for realtime:approval_requests_inbox after subscribe()`. The synchronous throw in `useEffect` + no ErrorBoundary → React 18 unmounts the whole tree → blank inbox screen.
- **Diagnostic**: chrome-devtools-mcp `list_console_messages` after clicking Persetujuan surfaced the exact error. Sidebar badge correctly showed "1 permintaan menunggu" — ruling out auth/RLS/PostgREST. Session 2 dossier (curl, psql, role grants) was on the right diagnostic level but missed the realtime subscribe path; one shot of console messages from the live tab would have caught it on session 1.
- **Fix**: Suffix the channel topic with a random token per call so each subscriber gets its own channel. Both Sidebar and ApprovalInboxScreen can now subscribe independently. `vite build`: clean.

## 2026-06-09 — Post-Overhaul Backlog Phase 3: sales overhaul polish — DONE

Closes all five sub-tasks the post-overhaul code review left for Phase 3. Five commits, two new migrations applied to prod DB via Session pooler. Build + Cloud Build deploy green.

- **Sub-task #3 — formatRp consolidation outside `penjualan/*`** (`980ce27`). KasirScreen had a third identical formatRp; replaced with `import { formatRp } from '../lib/format'`. The two stok screens had a DIFFERENT variant (sign-aware delta for adjustment quantities) — extracted as a new `formatRpDelta` in `format.ts` and both stok screens now import it. Every duplicate formatRp in the repo is gone.
- **Sub-task #4 — `payment_subtype` validation in `record_kasir_sale` RPC** (`a24836a`, migration `20260609000003`). Previously the RPC didn't validate `p_payment_subtype` or `p_dp_input_type`; invalid values reached the CHECK constraint with opaque Postgres errors. Atomicity was still correct (full rollback), but the operator had no idea what was wrong. Added explicit fail-fast `RAISE EXCEPTION` at the top of the function for both, matching the existing channel / payment_method validation pattern.
- **Sub-task #5 — `dp_input_type` schema alignment** (`a24836a`, migration `20260609000004`). `orders.chk_dp_input_type` allowed `AMOUNT|PERCENTAGE`; `kasir_transactions.chk_kasir_dp_input_type` allowed `AMOUNT|PERCENT`. Aligned both on `PERCENT` (matches `KasirDpInputType` TS type). Migration backfills any `PERCENTAGE` rows in orders (0 rows existed at apply time) then replaces the constraint. `orderService.createWalkinDraft` TS signature updated to `'AMOUNT' | 'PERCENT'`.
- **Sub-task #1 — Sunset `SaleModal`** (`837541a`). Reviewer Important #3. KasirScreen's right-panel kartu cards (Walk-in / Tokopedia / Grosir) used to open the legacy `SaleModal` in-place while the green header quick-action button went to `PenjualanBaruScreen`. Two paths → schema drift waiting to happen. Refactored: `App.tsx` tracks a `penjualanInitialChannel` state and plumbs it into `PenjualanBaruScreen.initialChannel` (the prop existed but was unused); `KasirScreen.onOpenPenjualanBaru` widened to `(channel?: KasirChannel) => void`; kartu cards now call `onOpenPenjualanBaru?.(ch)` instead of `setShowSaleModal(ch)`. Deleted `showSaleModal` state, the `<SaleModal>` mount JSX, the full `SaleModal` function + `SaleModalProps` interface (~378 lines, every responsibility lived in `PenjualanBaruScreen` already). Net: +19 / -402 lines.
- **Sub-task #2 — Vitest integration test for the save flow** (`f9198bc`). Added two tests to the existing `tests/integration/sales-recording.test.ts`: `record_kasir_sale RPC inserts with server-generated invoice + hpp_total` and `record_kasir_sale RPC rejects unknown payment_subtype before any side effect`. Both pass locally when `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` is exported. **Discovered pre-existing test infra gap**: the file's `beforeAll` seeds via service_role and cleanup uses `.delete()` — both need `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` in the env Vitest loads. Currently that key lives in `backend-go/.env` but NOT in the root `.env`; root-level vitest loads root .env and the whole suite errors out with RLS violations. This affected the existing 18 tests too — they apparently never ran in this branch. Not blocking, but worth flagging for follow-up (copy or symlink the key, or update the test to also load backend-go/.env).
- **Reviewer findings status after Phase 3**: Critical 2/2 ✅, Important 6/6 ✅ (#3 SaleModal sunset closed here, not deferred), Minor 5/5 ✅. The "promote `mark_walkin_order_paid` pattern" recommendation was satisfied by `record_kasir_sale` in Phase A. Integration-test recommendation satisfied at both the TS (this commit) and Go (Phase A) layers.

## 2026-06-09 — Post-Overhaul Backlog Phase 2: WIB timezone catch-up — DONE

The original `2026-06-05-wib-timezone-fix.md` plan had already landed for `supabaseClient.ts` internals + `LaporanScreen.tsx`. But ~13 NEW call sites of `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (and the `new Date(year, month, X)` variants) appeared since that plan was written — mostly from the Sales Recording Overhaul + Pembelian PO/PDF + Rekonsiliasi work. This commit catches them up.

- **Root cause refresher**: `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` returns the UTC calendar date. In WIB (UTC+7) anytime after 17:00 local, UTC has rolled over to H+1 — so the sale or expense is filed under tomorrow's date. The same buggy idiom applied to `new Date(year, month, 1).toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (month-end query bounds) returned the previous day, silently truncating monthly reconciliation queries by ~24h.
- **Helper move**: relocated `wibDateString(date?: Date): string` from a private function inside `supabaseClient.ts:409` to an exported helper in `src/lib/format.ts` (joining `formatRp` extracted in the Phase Minor cleanup). Same `toLocaleDateString('en-CA', { timeZone: 'Asia/Jakarta' })` impl — guaranteed ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` per spec.
- **Sites fixed (13 across 8 files)**:
  - `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts` — drop local `wibDateString`, re-import from `format`. Fix 3 `new Date(year, month, 1).toISOString().slice(0, 10)` sites in `listOrdersForPeriod`, `listBankLinesForPeriod`, `listCashBatches`.
  - `src/lib/pembelianService.ts` — `todayDate` + `monthEndDate` computations.
  - `src/components/PenjualanBaruScreen.tsx` — `today` inside `handleSave` (the most user-impacting site: every sale after 17:00 WIB used to land on H+1).
  - `src/components/PembelianScreen.tsx` — `today` for `isOverdue` predicate.
  - `src/components/rekonsiliasi/UploadPDFModal.tsx` — month-end `end` bound.
  - `src/components/rekonsiliasi/POSellThrough.tsx` — exclusive month `end` bound.
  - `src/components/pembelian/PurchaseOrderFormPage.tsx` — `isPastDate` comparison.
  - `src/components/pembelian/MarkAsPaidModal.tsx` — kasir expense `date`.
  - `src/components/pembelian/ReceiveGoodsModal.tsx` — receive `today`.
- **Intentionally not touched**: `ReceiveGoodsModal.tsx:19` inside `addDays(dateStr, days)` keeps `.toISOString().slice(0, 10)` — input is already a `YYYY-MM-DD` WIB string from `wibDateString()`, internal arithmetic stays in UTC offset-free math, no TZ drift. Also `format.ts` comments mention the buggy idiom to explain why the helper exists; those are intentional doc text.
- **Verification**: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `grep -rn "toISOString().slice(0, 10)" src/` returns only the 2 doc comments in `format.ts` + the safe `addDays` internal — every user-impacting call site is now WIB-aware.
- **Next**: Phase 3 (sales overhaul polish — sunset SaleModal, integration test, formatRp consolidation outside penjualan/*, payment_subtype validation, dp_input_type alignment).

## 2026-06-09 — Sales Recording Overhaul, Phase A: atomic `record_kasir_sale` RPC — DONE (migration pending apply)

- **Goal**: Close Critical #1 + #2 + Important #5 from the end-to-end code review of the Sales Recording Overhaul. The pre-existing save path (`nextInvoiceNumber → Promise.all(deductFifo) → insertSaleTransaction → decrementStock`) was non-atomic and could (a) strand `stock_lots.qty_remaining` on partial failure, (b) race on shared lots when the same SKU appeared twice in cart, (c) burn the per-(channel,date) invoice counter on a failed insert (audit-grade gap).
- **Files**:
  - `supabase/migrations/20260609000001_record_kasir_sale_rpc.sql` (new) — `record_kasir_sale(p_date, p_channel, p_items, …)` `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC. Inside one transaction: validates inputs → find-or-create customer (ON CONFLICT on `customers.wa_number`) → reserves invoice number via `next_kasir_number` → aggregates `p_items` by `(sku, warehouse)` → calls `decrement_stock` + `deduct_stock_fifo` ONCE per aggregate group (mirrors the `mark_walkin_order_paid` pattern) → distributes aggregate FIFO cost proportionally to per-line `hpp_per_unit` → inserts `kasir_transactions` row with `status = (p_payment_type='DP' ? 'AWAITING_LUNAS' : 'PAID')`. Any failure rolls back EVERYTHING including the counter increment. Whitelist: channel ∈ `walkin|tokopedia|grosir|whatsapp`, payment_method ∈ `cash|transfer|qris|edc` (already supports EDC, so Important #7 is also closed by this single RPC for kasir sales — `mark_walkin_order_paid` still needs its own update under Phase D).
  - `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts` — replaced `insertSaleTransaction` with `recordSale(input: RecordKasirSaleInput): Promise<KasirTransaction>` (thin RPC wrapper), removed `nextInvoiceNumber` (RPC computes invoice internally), removed `NewSaleTransaction` import.
  - `src/types.ts` — `NewSaleTransaction` renamed to `RecordKasirSaleInput`, dropped fields `hpp_total` and `invoice_number` (both computed server-side now).
  - `src/components/PenjualanBaruScreen.tsx` — `handleSave` collapsed from ~70 lines (with the "NOTE: non-atomic" caveat comment) to a single `kasirService.recordSale` call. Dropped the redundant client-side `customersService.createCustomer` follow-up (reviewer Minor #11) since the RPC handles customer find-or-create. Dropped `purchaseOrderService` import.
  - `src/components/KasirScreen.tsx` — `SaleModal.handleSave` collapsed the same way. The kartu-channel flow (Walk-in/Tokopedia/Grosir cards on the right panel) keeps `SaleModal` as its UI, but its save path is now atomic via the same RPC. Dropped `purchaseOrderService` import.
- **Tests** (`backend-go/internal/db/record_kasir_sale_test.go`, NEW, 3 tests — will PASS once migration is applied):
  - `TestRecordKasirSale_HappyPath` — single SKU, qty=3. Asserts `stocks.stock_atas` 10→7, `stock_lots.qty_remaining` 10→7, `hpp_total=3000`, invoice matches `WLK-YYYYMMDD-\d{3}`, items[].hpp_per_unit=1000 (= seeded lot unit_cost), exactly 2 `stock_movements` rows (decrement_stock + deduct_stock_fifo) sharing `related_doc_id = invoice_number`.
  - `TestRecordKasirSale_RollsBackOnInvalidPayment` — call with `payment_method='bitcoin'` raises. Asserts NO side effect: `stock_atas` still 10, `stock_lots.qty_remaining` still 10, `kasir_counters.counter` unchanged, no `kasir_transactions` row inserted. Regression guard for the Critical #1 atomicity claim.
  - `TestRecordKasirSale_AggregatesSameSKU` — same SKU + warehouse in two lines (qty=2 and qty=3). Asserts aggregate behavior: `stock_atas` 10→5, `stock_lots` 10→5, exactly 2 `stock_movements` rows (proof: per-aggregate, not per-line). Both output items carry the same averaged `hpp_per_unit`. Regression guard for Critical #2 (the FIFO race on Promise.all).
- **Migration NOT yet applied** to the DB this session — user preference: write migration only, defer apply to user via psql per the T1-T3 pengawasan pattern. Tests will fail with `pq: function public.record_kasir_sale(…) does not exist` until apply.
- **Verification**: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `go vet ./internal/db/` clean. Test run confirms function-not-yet-exists error — exactly the expected pre-apply state.
- **Reviewer findings status after Phase A**: Critical #1 + #2 → closed. Important #5 (burned invoice number) → closed. The kartu-channel SaleModal path is now atomic via the same RPC even though the modal UI was kept per user scope decision (sunset of SaleModal was explicitly deferred).
- **Next**: Phase B (lunas date fix in SalesInvoicePDF), Phase C (createWalkinDraft field expansion), Phase D (mark_walkin_order_paid EDC whitelist), Phase E (salesEntries pagination).

## 2026-06-09 — Persetujuan menu "shows blank" — ACTUAL root cause: zero pending approvals in DB — NO CODE CHANGE

- **Symptom (user-reported)**: User reported clicking Persetujuan on the deployed Cloud Run frontend rendered an "empty" / "blank" main panel. Shared a `{"message":"No API key found in request"}` error JSON in chat which initially sent the investigation down a header-stripping rabbit hole.
- **Investigation phases (in order, and what each ruled out)**:
  1. **Bundle code verified**: deployed `index-Wi9PYk0b.js` (revision 00013) embeds Supabase URL + anon JWT as constants and constructs the supabase-js client correctly. Ruled out a missing-key build issue.
  2. **Library reproduction in Node**: supabase-js v2.106.2 + same URL/key locally → apikey header is sent. Ruled out a library bug.
  3. **CORS preflight verified**: Supabase OPTIONS on `/rest/v1/approval_requests` returns `access-control-allow-headers: apikey,authorization,x-client-info,accept-profile` + `access-control-allow-origin: *`. Ruled out CORS misconfig.
  4. **Headless-Chrome browser reproduction**: Drove the LIVE deployed app with puppeteer-core + installed Chrome 148 and captured outgoing requests. apikey header IS sent on every Supabase REST call. Ruled out a browser-specific runtime bug in supabase-js-web/2.106.2.
  5. **Extended test (`/tmp/test_approval.mjs`)**: injected a `from('approval_requests').select('*').eq('status','pending')` query inside the loaded deployed page → HTTP 200 with body `[]`. **Zero pending rows.**
  6. **Direct REST verification**: `curl ".../approval_requests?select=count&status=eq.pending" -H "apikey: …" -H "Prefer: count=exact"` → `[{"count":0}]`. Recent rows in the table are all `expired` or `approved` (30-min auto-expiry from yesterday).
- **Actual root cause**: The screen was rendering its legitimate empty state ("Semua permintaan sudah diputuskan." at `ApprovalInboxScreen.tsx:215-219`) because `listPendingApprovals()` correctly returned `[]` — there are zero pending approvals in the DB right now. The non-technical user read the empty UI (title + filter pills + "all decided" message) as "blank". The earlier "No API key found" error was either a transient session issue or a pasted artifact — the live app sends apikey correctly and the relevant requests succeed.
- **Lesson learned**: When a non-technical user says "blank", verify the DB state via a 30-second `curl … Prefer: count=exact` BEFORE chasing client-side errors. The advisor flagged this exact failure mode two turns into the chase ("a non-technical user might call the empty state blank"); the chase continued anyway. Cost: hours of bundle-spelunking that an earlier `curl` would have prevented.
- **What the user can do to verify the screen works**: create a pending approval first (e.g. trigger a stock adjustment from Stok / AI Stock Manager that requires owner approval), then the inbox will render that row with Setujui / Tolak action buttons.
- **Verification artifacts retained at `/tmp/test_deployed.mjs` and `/tmp/test_approval.mjs`** — puppeteer-core scripts that load the live deployed app and inspect supabase.co requests + responses. Reusable for future "is this a deploy bug or a user-env / data-state issue?" triage.

## 2026-06-08 — Stock Fraud Phase 4, Task 3: `v_pengawasan_outflow_outliers` view — DONE

- **Goal**: Third Pengawasan view — flags SKUs whose last-7-day outflow exceeds 3× their 90-day daily-average × 7. Surfaces suspicious surges (a normally-quiet SKU suddenly bleeding inventory) that no single adjustment or sale row would flag in isolation. Columns: `sku`, `name`, `sum_7d`, `avg_daily_90d`, `multiplier`.
- **Files**: `supabase/migrations/20260607000052_outflow_outliers_view.sql` (new — separate file per task brief, NOT appended to `…050`; T2 set the one-file-per-task pattern), `backend-go/internal/db/pengawasan_test.go` (appended 2 tests + `database/sql` & `errors` imports), `backend-go/internal/db/testhelpers.go` (added `SeedStockMovement`).
- **View**: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.v_pengawasan_outflow_outliers AS WITH outflow_7 AS (SELECT sku, SUM(ABS(qty_delta))::numeric AS sum_7d FROM stock_movements WHERE qty_delta < 0 AND created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '7 days' GROUP BY sku), avg_90 AS (SELECT sku, SUM(ABS(qty_delta))::numeric / 90.0 AS avg_daily_90d FROM stock_movements WHERE qty_delta < 0 AND created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '90 days' GROUP BY sku) SELECT o.sku, s.name, o.sum_7d, a.avg_daily_90d, o.sum_7d / NULLIF(a.avg_daily_90d * 7, 0) AS multiplier FROM outflow_7 o JOIN avg_90 a USING (sku) JOIN stocks s ON s.sku = o.sku WHERE o.sum_7d > 3 * a.avg_daily_90d * 7;`. `GRANT SELECT … TO authenticated`. No `ORDER BY` in the view — consumers (dashboard, poller) sort by `multiplier DESC` at query time.
- **Math derivation**: `multiplier = sum_7d / (avg_daily_90d × 7)`. The filter `sum_7d > 3 × avg_daily_90d × 7` is the equivalent of `multiplier > 3`. NULLIF guards the divisor in case avg_daily_90d collapses to 0 (defensive — the inner JOIN already drops SKUs with no 90d outflow).
- **Tests (2, both PASS)**:
  - `TestPengawasanView_OutflowOutliers_FlagsHotSKU` — seeds 80 historical outflows of `-1` at `days_ago=8..87` (outside 7d window, inside 90d window) + `-50` today. `sum_7d=50`, `sum_90d=130`, `avg_daily_90d≈1.444`, `multiplier≈4.94` → flagged. Asserts `multiplier > 3`.
  - `TestPengawasanView_OutflowOutliers_ExcludesNormalSKU` — seeds `-1`/day for 90 consecutive days. `sum_7d=7`, `threshold=21`. Asserts `sql.ErrNoRows` (view excludes the SKU).
- **Helper**: `SeedStockMovement(sku, warehouse, qtyDelta, createdAt)` — direct INSERT into `stock_movements` with `source='adjustment'`, `qty_before=100`, `qty_after=100+delta` to satisfy `chk_qty_math`, baseline actor UUID `00000000-…-001`, actor_role `system_test`. The crucial bit is `created_at` is explicitly passed (not defaulted to `now()`) so tests can seed historical points across the 7d/90d boundaries.
- **Stock_movements table is append-only with REVOKE UPDATE/DELETE + immutability trigger** — direct INSERT still works for the test connection (service_role-equivalent DSN). Per-test unique SKUs (`T3-OUT-HOT-<unixnano>`, `T3-OUT-NORMAL-<unixnano>`) prevent reruns from compounding on the shared Supabase test DB (since rows can't be deleted between runs).
- **Threshold tuning note**: The plan's math claimed `multiplier ≈ 7.1` for the positive test, but that figure ignores the today-event contribution to the 90d sum. Actual multiplier is `≈4.94` (still well above the `> 3` flag threshold). The test asserts `mult > 3`, not a specific value, so the discrepancy is moot for the assertion — but worth documenting so a future reader doesn't think the math drifted.
- **Migration applied** via `psql` (same `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/libpq/18.4/bin/psql` + `PGPASSWORD` pattern T1/T2 used).
- **Verification**: `go test ./internal/db/ -run TestPengawasanView -v` — all 6 pengawasan tests green (102.7s; the 2 new T3 tests dominate at ~38s + ~41s because each seeds 80–90 movement rows). `go vet ./...` clean, `go build ./...` clean.
- **Next**: Phase 4 Task 4 — Transfer aging view.

## 2026-06-08 — Stock Fraud Phase 4, Task 2: `v_pengawasan_kasir_discount_7d` view — DONE

- **Goal**: Second Pengawasan view — per-cashier discount aggregate over the last 7 days. Surfaces cashiers giving away unusual margin via free-form unit_price entry (`discount = stocks.price - kti.unit_price`, summed across line items in committed sales). Columns: `cashier_user_id`, `cashier_name`, `total_discount_rp`, `total_revenue_rp`, `discount_pct_of_revenue`.
- **Files**: `supabase/migrations/20260607000051_kasir_discount_view.sql` (new — separate file per task brief, NOT appended to `…050`), `backend-go/internal/db/pengawasan_test.go` (appended 2 tests + 1 const), `backend-go/internal/db/testhelpers.go` (added `SeedAdminUser`, `SeedStockWithPrice`, `SeedKasirTransaction` plus `KasirTxSeed` / `KasirTxItem` types and `encoding/json` import).
- **Schema reality reconcile** (plan vs. live DB diverged — verified via `\d public.kasir_transactions`):
  - Plan said cashier identity column is `cashier_user_id` (Phase 3b). Live schema has `created_by UUID` only — `cashier_user_id` never landed. View uses `kt.created_by AS cashier_user_id` so the contract documented in the spec (and the test's `WHERE cashier_user_id = $1`) is preserved without inventing a new physical column.
  - Plan said `WHERE status = 'committed'`. Live CHECK constraint allows only `PAID | AWAITING_LUNAS | COMPLETED | CANCELLED`. View filters `status IN ('PAID', 'COMPLETED')` — the realized-sale set where discount is booked + revenue recognised. AWAITING_LUNAS (DP/partial — discount still mutable) and CANCELLED excluded.
  - Added explicit `kt.type = 'income'` guard — expense rows have empty items, but filtering at kt scope is safer than relying on `jsonb_to_recordset` yielding zero rows.
- **View**: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.v_pengawasan_kasir_discount_7d AS SELECT … FROM kasir_transactions kt JOIN LATERAL jsonb_to_recordset(kt.items) AS kti(sku TEXT, unit_price NUMERIC, qty INT) ON TRUE JOIN stocks s ON s.sku = kti.sku LEFT JOIN admin_users au ON au.id = kt.created_by WHERE kt.type='income' AND kt.status IN ('PAID','COMPLETED') AND kt.created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '7 days' GROUP BY kt.created_by, au.name`. `CASE WHEN SUM(revenue) > 0 THEN … ELSE 0 END` guards pct division. `GRANT SELECT … TO authenticated`.
- **Tests (2, both PASS)**:
  - `TestPengawasanView_KasirDiscount_7d_AggregatesCorrectly` — one cashier, two committed sales: `1×10000` (no discount) + `2×7000` (3000 discount each). Asserts `total_discount_rp=6000`, `total_revenue_rp=24000`, `discount_pct_of_revenue ≈ 0.25` (tolerance 0.249–0.251).
  - `TestPengawasanView_KasirDiscount_7d_FiltersOutOlder` — recent `1×7000` + identical row dated `now() - 8 days`. Asserts totals come from the recent row only (`disc=3000`, `rev=7000`) — proves the 7d window cutoff.
- **Helpers**:
  - `SeedAdminUser(name, role)` — `INSERT INTO admin_users (name, role) RETURNING id`. Defaults role to `'Staff Admin Toko'` if empty.
  - `SeedStockWithPrice(sku, price)` — `ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE SET price` so re-runs are deterministic. Distinct from `SeedStockWithHPP` (T1) which sets `harga_modal`.
  - `SeedKasirTransaction(KasirTxSeed{CreatedBy, Status, CreatedAt, Items})` — marshals items via `encoding/json` to JSONB, derives subtotal/total_amount from items so the row is self-consistent. Hardcoded `type='income'`, `channel='walkin'`, `payment_type='FULL'`, `payment_method='cash'`, `hpp_total=0` — all valid against the live CHECK constraints. `CreatedAt` lets the second test back-date a row 8 days for the cutoff assertion.
  - `KasirTxItem` struct tags `json:"sku"`, `json:"unit_price"`, `json:"qty"` — match the column names the view's `jsonb_to_recordset` extracts.
- **Per-test unique fixtures**: `T2-KD-<unixnano>`, `T2-KD-OLD-<unixnano>`, plus `Test Kasir <unixnano>` names — avoid cross-test pollution against the shared Supabase test DB.
- **Migration applied** via `psql` (same `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/libpq/18.4/bin/psql` + `PGPASSWORD` pattern T1 used).

Routed error-case toasts to `'warning'` to match — this is the same convention every other modal in `src/components/` follows. The plan is authoritative; the inbox row (T24's `ApprovalRequestRow` already shows "Nilai: Rp X" via `summarisePayload`) is where the Owner sees the rupiah impact — duplicating it in the requester modal would be cosmetic. If product wants it, it's a 3-line addition (read `item.harga_modal` from the prop, compute, render).

Followed the plan — the parent (Stock Manager) already knows which warehouse the user clicked on (the SKU row shows separate "Atas: 12 / Bawah: 4" columns), so the modal just receives the chosen warehouse. Will be wired in T28 (StockManagerScreen integration) once the per-SKU action menu is decided. (2) Photo upload is sequential, not parallel — if a user uploads 5 large photos this could feel slow on Indonesian 4G. Sequential is safer (atomic failure mode: if photo 3 fails, photos 1-2 are orphans in the bucket, but the RPC never fires so no partial DB state). Phase 2c can add a janitor cron if orphan accumulation becomes a problem. (3) No file-size/dimension validation client-side — relies on Supabase Storage's upload limits (50MB default). ## 2026-06-08 — Stock Fraud Phase 2, Task 20: Wire webhook + poller into main.go — DONE

- **Goal**: Glue the T18 webhook handler and T19 expiry poller into `backend-go/main.go` so the daemon actually serves the `/api/approval/wa-webhook` route and runs the per-minute auto-expiry sweep. Also land the 5 concrete `*db.Client` methods needed for the handler's `api.ApprovalStore` interface (`IsActiveOwnerWANumber`, `FirstOwnerAdminUserID`, `FindApprovalByWAMessageID`, `LatestPendingApprovalID`, `DecideViaWAButton`) plus integration tests for each.
- **Files**: `backend-go/internal/db/approvals.go` (5 new methods, follows the existing `database/sql` style — Null* scans, sql.ErrNoRows for missing keys), `backend-go/internal/db/approvals_test.go` (6 new integration tests: happy + 3 negatives on owner-wa check, deterministic Owner pick, find-by-msg-id + missing, latest-pending freshness, RPC wrapper happy path + error-passthrough), `backend-go/main.go` (added `approvalStoreAdapter` wrapper struct + 2 imports for `internal/api` and `internal/approvals`, wired `approvals.NewPoller(dbClient).Start(ctx)` and `mux.Handle("/api/approval/wa-webhook", ...)` right after the existing heartbeat poller, matching the established Start(ctx) pattern).
- **Why the adapter lives in main.go rather than internal/db**: The T18 handler's `ApprovalStore` contract distinguishes "no row" via `api.ErrNoApproval`, but `internal/db` returning that sentinel would force a reverse import (internal/db → internal/api) that no other file in the package does. The advisor flagged this as the load-bearing decision. Option B preserves unidirectional layering: db returns `sql.ErrNoRows`, the main.go adapter translates. Only 2 of the 5 methods (`FindApprovalByWAMessageID`, `LatestPendingApprovalID`) need translation; the other 3 pass straight through.
- **Why the role-case asymmetry is correct**: `wa_recipients.role` is lowercase (`'owner'`/`'admin'` per migration `20260602000001`), while `admin_users.role` is Capitalised (`'Owner'` per the T13/T14 tests and Phase 1 admin schema). `IsActiveOwnerWANumber` queries the first, `FirstOwnerAdminUserID` queries the second — the SQL in each method matches its target table's case convention. The asymmetry is documented inline so a future maintainer doesn't "normalise" them and break the join.
- **Why deterministic-pick on `FirstOwnerAdminUserID`**: `ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 1` over `WHERE role='Owner'` gives a stable result even when multiple Owner rows coexist (test seeds + production setup wizard). The well-known low-uuid `00000000-…-099` test Owner sorts first, so the test asserts on that specific id rather than "any Owner uuid" — defensible because the integration DB always carries that seed from T11/T13/T14.
- **Why no main.go-specific test**: The wiring is glue (a closure, an adapter struct, two `Start(ctx)` calls). `go build ./...` clean + `go vet ./...` clean is sufficient verification; an HTTP integration test in main_test.go would have to spin up the full daemon stack (DB, WA, Gemini) and would mostly retest things the per-package tests already cover. The 5 new method tests + T18's handler tests + T19's poller tests collectively exercise the contract surfaces.
- **Why bundle the 5 methods + tests + main.go into one commit**: They're a single semantic unit — "T20 concrete satisfaction + wiring". Splitting would leave a transient intermediate state where the adapter type exists but its underlying methods don't compile yet, or the main.go references a not-yet-existing method. Bundled is the cleanest history.
- **Test output**: All 6 new T20 db tests pass (`TestIsActiveOwnerWANumber_HappyPathAndNegatives` 2.27s, `TestFirstOwnerAdminUserID_ReturnsKnownOwner` 1.22s, `TestFindApprovalByWAMessageID` 1.66s, `TestLatestPendingApprovalID` 1.33s, `TestDecideViaWAButton_HappyPath` 1.73s, `TestDecideViaWAButton_BadDecisionPassesErrorThrough` 1.66s). Full regression `go test ./internal/db/ ./internal/api/ ./internal/approvals/ -count=1 -p 1 -parallel 1` green: db package 117.8s, api 0.5s, approvals 0.6s. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean.
- **Concerns**: (1) The adapter's sql.ErrNoRows translation uses `==` rather than `errors.Is` — fine because `*db.Client` returns the raw sentinel from `QueryRow().Scan()` without wrapping, but if a future maintainer wraps with `fmt.Errorf("%w", ...)` the comparison would silently break. Keeping `==` consistent with `internal/db/approvals.go`'s `GetApprovalRequest` comment ("Returns sql.ErrNoRows when the id does not exist so callers can map directly to a 404 response"). (2) `LatestPendingApprovalID`'s test uses BIGSERIAL monotonicity + `-parallel 1` to guarantee determinism; the test comment notes the assumption so a future maintainer enabling parallelism doesn't get a flaky test. (3) The webhook has no HMAC/signature verification — the WA bridge daemon sits behind Cloud Run's internal mesh, so authentication is delegated to the network boundary. If Phase 3 exposes the webhook publicly, an `Authorization` check belongs in the handler (a T18 concern, not T20). (4) `ctx` in main.go is still `context.Background()` with no cancel — consistent with the heartbeat/follow-up pollers; the goroutine exits at process termination, which is the production contract. (5) Did NOT touch unrelated working-tree drift (`backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `src/components/pembelian/MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, untracked plan docs).

## 2026-06-08 — Stock Fraud Phase 2, Task 19: Expiry poller goroutine — DONE

- **Goal**: Land the background goroutine that wakes every 60s and calls the T14 `expire_pending_approvals()` RPC so 30-minute-stale `pending` rows auto-flip to `expired` without an Owner ever touching them. New package `backend-go/internal/approvals/` to hold this (and future) approval-side workers, plus a thin `Client.ExpirePendingApprovals(ctx)` method on `db.Client` so the poller depends on a one-method `Expirer` interface and tests can fake the DB without standing up Postgres.
- **Files**: `backend-go/internal/approvals/expiry_poller.go` (Poller + functional-options constructor + Start goroutine with ticker), `backend-go/internal/approvals/expiry_poller_test.go` (3 tests: ticks-and-calls / continues-on-error / stops-on-ctx-cancel — all using deterministic call-count synchronisation via a `signal` channel rather than wall-clock sleeps), `backend-go/internal/db/approvals.go` (added `ExpirePendingApprovals(ctx)` method calling the RPC via `QueryRowContext` so ctx cancel during shutdown aborts the in-flight call).
- **Why the user's expanded signature over the plan's two-test block**: The plan body at lines 2584-2687 of `2026-06-07-stock-fraud-phase2.md` sketches a minimal `NewExpiryPoller(e, interval).Run(ctx)` with a 1-test sleep-then-cancel suite. The task description's "Critical context" upgrades the seam to functional options (`WithPeriod`, `WithLogger`, `WithOnStop`), renames `Run` to `Start` to mirror `heartbeat.Poller.Start` (the explicit pattern reference), pins the log format (`[APPROVALS] expired N requests`), and mandates a 3-test floor covering the failure modes (error continuation, ctx cancel exit). That section is more specific and reflects what T20's main.go wiring will actually call (`poller.Start(ctx)`, not `go poller.Run(ctx)`). The plan's "authoritative" anchor binds the task identity (T19, package path, RPC, file names, the Expirer interface seam) — not the literal code block. Combined: plan's structural choices (`internal/approvals/`, narrow Expirer interface, RPC at the back), description's behavioural surface (Start vs Run, log format, 3-test floor).
- **Why deterministic waitForCalls instead of `time.Sleep(170ms)`**: The plan's test relies on wall-clock sleep with a "got between 2 and 5 calls" tolerance — flaky on a busy CI runner where a 50ms ticker can stall for 100ms+. Using a buffered `signal` channel that the fake pushes to on every call and a `waitForCalls(n, timeout)` helper lets the test block on the *event* (Nth call happened) rather than a wall-clock interval, with a generous 2s safety timeout for catastrophic stalls. The cancel test then explicitly samples the counter, sleeps 50ms, re-samples, and asserts no growth — that catches a goroutine that ignored ctx cancel.
- **Why `WithOnStop` is a test-only knob**: Detecting that a goroutine actually returned (vs just stopped ticking because the ticker channel went idle) is fundamentally a synchronisation problem. Production code doesn't care — main.go's process is exiting anyway when ctx cancels. But the test needs a deterministic signal, so the constructor accepts an optional `func()` that the goroutine fires from a `defer` right before returning. Documented as test-only in the option's doc comment so a future contributor doesn't mistake it for a shutdown hook.
- **Why `QueryRowContext` in `Client.ExpirePendingApprovals`**: The rest of `db/approvals.go` uses the non-context `c.DB.Query` / `c.DB.QueryRow` variants (matching the package's pre-Phase-2 style). But this method is called from a background goroutine that *must* honour ctx cancel during shutdown, otherwise a slow RPC will pin the connection past the process's exit and dirty the connection pool's close. Wiring ctx through is the smaller cost; the rest of the file's callers were synchronous HTTP handlers where the request ctx already bounded the call duration.
- **Concerns**: (1) The integration test for the new `ExpirePendingApprovals` method on `db.Client` is *not* in this commit — the existing `TestExpirePendingApprovals_FlipsExpiredRows` already covers the RPC's behaviour end-to-end by calling `SELECT public.expire_pending_approvals()` directly, and the new Go method is a one-line wrapper; adding a parallel "test the Go method" would be coverage theatre. T20's wiring will exercise the method via the real poller anyway. (2) The fake clock in `backend-go/internal/whatsapp/clock.go` was *not* used — that abstraction is built for `AfterFunc` debounce semantics, not for advancing a `time.Ticker`, and adapting it would have been more code than the fast-period real-ticker approach. The 25ms period keeps the test under 100ms in steady state. (3) `defaultPeriod` is hard-coded to `time.Minute` per the plan; if Phase 4 wants Owner-configurable cadence the constant would need to migrate into `notification_config`, but that's out of scope. (4) Did NOT touch unrelated working-tree drift (`backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `src/components/pembelian/MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, untracked plan docs).
- **Next**: Task 20 of Phase 2 — wire the webhook handler (T18) and the expiry poller (T19) into `backend-go/main.go` with the `dbDeciderAdapter` and `poller.Start(ctx)` call.

## 2026-06-08 — Stock Fraud Phase 2, Task 18: HTTP webhook `/api/approval/wa-webhook` — DONE

- **Goal**: Land the inbound HTTP endpoint the WA bridge daemon POSTs to when an Owner replies to (or button-taps on) Calista's approval card. Endpoint resolves the sender's authority (active Owner in `wa_recipients`), parses the free-text decision ("1"/"2"/"setuju"/"tolak"/…), maps the in-reply-to message id back to an `approval_requests` row (with fallback to the latest pending), and invokes T14's `decide_via_wa_button(approval_id, decision, owner_user_id)` RPC. Status-code-rich so the bridge's retry policy can distinguish "already decided" (409, don't retry) from a generic server fault (500, retry).
- **What — `backend-go/internal/api/approval_webhook.go` (NEW)**: New `internal/api/` package (first file). Exposes (a) `ApprovalStore` interface with five hooks — `IsActiveOwnerWANumber`, `FirstOwnerAdminUserID`, `FindApprovalByWAMessageID`, `LatestPendingApprovalID`, `DecideViaWAButton` — to keep the handler decoupled from `*db.Client` so tests inject a fake without standing up Postgres; (b) `ErrNoApproval` sentinel that real `*db` implementations return (or wrap) when a lookup misses, so the handler doesn't have to import `database/sql` to switch on `sql.ErrNoRows`; (c) `NewApprovalWebhookHandler(ApprovalStore) http.Handler` returning a `*approvalWebhookHandler` whose `ServeHTTP` runs the 5-step pipeline (Owner gate → parse decision → resolve approval id → resolve Owner admin_users.id → fire RPC). Decision vocabulary is deliberately small: `"1"|"setuju"|"approve"|"approved"|"ya"|"ok"` → `"approved"`; `"2"|"tolak"|"reject"|"rejected"|"tidak"|"no"` → `"rejected"`. JID normalisation strips `@s.whatsapp.net` (or any `@` variant) before comparing against `wa_recipients.wa_number` which stores bare digits per the existing `models.WaRecipient.WANumber` shape and `db.GetActiveRecipients`'s SQL. RPC error families are pattern-matched on the substring the migration emits — `"is not pending or does not exist"` → 409, `"not authorized"` → 403 (defence-in-depth fallback after the handler's own Owner gate) — anything else falls through to 500.
- **What — `backend-go/internal/api/approval_webhook_test.go` (NEW)**: Seven tests covering every status branch. `TestApprovalWebhook_OwnerApproves` pins the happy path including the JID-normalisation assertion (the fake's `isOwnerFn` fails the test if it receives `"…@s.whatsapp.net"` instead of `"6281234567890"`) and asserts the `decide_via_wa_button` call received id=42, decision="approved", owner uuid="…0099". `TestApprovalWebhook_OwnerRejects` mirrors with text="2" → "rejected". `TestApprovalWebhook_NonOwner` confirms 403 AND that `DecideViaWAButton` was never invoked — so a non-Owner POST can't even reach the RPC's own role gate. `TestApprovalWebhook_AmbiguousText` confirms 400 on `"halo apa kabar"` AND that `DecideViaWAButton` was never invoked — so casual Owner chatter can't silently flip the latest-pending fallback. `TestApprovalWebhook_NoMatchingApproval` confirms 404 when both `in_reply_to` is absent AND `LatestPendingApprovalID` returns `ErrNoApproval`. `TestApprovalWebhook_AlreadyDecided` injects the exact migration error string (`"pq: approval_requests 99 is not pending or does not exist"`) and asserts 409. `TestApprovalWebhook_FallbackToLatestPending` confirms that when `in_reply_to` is absent the handler queries `LatestPendingApprovalID` (not 404 immediately) — pins the casual-reply UX so we don't regress to "404 unless the reply quotes the card".
- **Why the expanded spec from the task description over the plan's two-test block**: The plan body at lines 2433-2580 of `2026-06-07-stock-fraud-phase2.md` sketches a simpler `button_payload: "approve:42"`-style webhook with a 2-test suite (happy path + 400 on bad payload) — which would have shipped a handler that can't parse a plain `"setuju"` reply from an Owner who didn't tap the button. The task description's "Critical context" enumerates the richer JSON shape (`from`, `text`, `in_reply_to`), six status codes, the Owner-in-`wa_recipients` gate, the decision vocabulary, and the 5-test floor — that section is more specific and reflects the actual product requirement (Indonesian Owners type "setuju", not "approve:42"). The plan's "authoritative" anchor binds the task identity (T18, the file path, the package, the Decider-style interface decoupling) — not the literal code block. Read `db.GetActiveRecipients` (`internal/db/wa_recipients.go:7`) — `SELECT wa_number FROM wa_recipients` with no suffix munging. Compared against `handler.go:68` where customer JIDs are produced by `evt.Info.Sender.ToNonAD().String()` (which includes `@s.whatsapp.net`) and threaded through to `wa_recipients`-using callers via `senderPhone` — confirming that the recipient table holds the bare-digits form. ## 2026-06-08 — Stock Fraud Phase 2, Task 16: Go helper `internal/db/approvals.go` — DONE

- **Goal**: Land typed Go reader helpers over `public.approval_requests` so the next three tasks (T17 WA approval sender, T18 webhook handler, T19 expiry poller) plus the Phase 4 Owner dashboard can build on a single source of truth instead of re-rolling SQL each. Four helpers total: `ListPendingApprovalRequests(requestedBy string)`, `GetApprovalRequest(id int64)`, `SetWaMessageID(id, msgID)`, `CountPendingApprovalsForOwner()`.
- **What — `backend-go/internal/db/approvals.go` (NEW)**: One `ApprovalRequest` struct mirroring the 11 columns from the …007 schema (id, request_type, payload, requested_by, requested_at, expires_at, status, decided_by, decided_at, decision_channel, wa_message_id). Nullable columns use `sql.Null*` wrappers rather than pointers to match the rest of `internal/db` (see `bank_config.go`). Payload exposed as raw `[]byte` JSON — each caller parses a different request-type-specific schema (adjustment vs. opname vs. price_change vs. kasir_*) so a shared decode here would just churn. Helpers all use the `c.DB.Query/QueryRow/Exec` pattern from the existing reader files (heartbeat.go, bank_config.go); the plan's `c.Query(ctx, ...)` API doesn't exist on this `Client`, so the prompt's "Minimum API surface" was the source of truth. A private `scanApprovalRequest` helper plus a single `approvalRequestColumns` string constant keep the column list in one place so adding a column means changing ONE spot.
- **What — migration `supabase/migrations/20260607000022_set_wa_message_id.sql` (NEW)**: SECURITY DEFINER RPC `public._set_wa_message_id(p_id BIGINT, p_wa_message_id TEXT) RETURNS VOID`. Body is a single UPDATE with `WHERE id = p_id AND wa_message_id IS NULL` — the IS NULL guard makes the call idempotent: a Calista retry after a transient WA send error that actually delivered does NOT clobber the recorded id. No NOT FOUND check on purpose — both "already set" and "row gone" are legitimate races the sender shouldn't have to handle. REVOKE EXECUTE from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated; service_role keeps EXECUTE by ownership. This encapsulation is consistency-driven not security-driven — service_role's REVOKE bypass plus the disabled UPDATE trigger means a raw UPDATE would also work, but every other approval mutation flows through a postgres-owned function, and a future auditor shouldn't have to remember that `wa_message_id` is the one exception.
- **Test isolation pattern (per advisor)**: The integration DB carries pending rows leftover from T1-T14 (T14's expire test seeds extras, T13's PIN tests too), so a naive `CountPendingApprovalsForOwner()==0` baseline would flap. Each T16 test mints a unique `requested_by` UUID via `uniqueT16UUID(time.Now().UnixNano())` (zero-prefixed sentinel + nanosecond tail; 48 bits of nanos give ~9 years before wraparound), then either passes that UUID to `ListPendingApprovalRequests` for fenced filtering or measures a delta-from-baseline for the unfilterable `CountPendingApprovalsForOwner`. The `TestGetApprovalRequest` "missing id → ErrNoRows" path uses `9_000_000_000_000_000_000` — well beyond what BIGSERIAL could have reached in this test run.
- **Why the spec divergence from the plan body**: The plan's Step 1 code block (lines 2225-2282) proposed (a) `c.Query(ctx, ...)` / `c.Exec(ctx, ...)` methods that don't exist on `Client` (it's `c.DB.Query(...)`), (b) `uuid.UUID` typed fields requiring a `github.com/google/uuid` import the package doesn't carry today, and (c) helpers (`ListPendingForOwner`, `DecideViaWAButton`, `ExpirePendingApprovals`) that duplicate the T14 SQL wrappers rather than the read-side helpers T17/18/19 need. The task description's "Critical context / Minimum API surface" — `database/sql` + lib/pq, `sql.NullString`/`sql.NullTime`, the four exact helper names — was used as authoritative. The plan's "smoke test" was replaced with the four targeted unit tests the description specified.
- **Test results**: Targeted `go test ./internal/db/ -run "TestListPendingApprovalRequests|TestGetApprovalRequest|TestSetWaMessageID|TestCountPendingApprovalsForOwner" -v -count=1` — all 4 PASS in 7.8s. Full regression `go test ./internal/db/ -count=1 -p 1 -parallel 1` PASS in 108s. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean.
- **Concerns**: (1) `CountPendingApprovalsForOwner`'s name is aspirational — per the spec it's a global `COUNT(*) WHERE status='pending'` with no Owner-role join. If a future task wants a true per-Owner-route count (e.g. multi-Owner deployments) the helper will need to grow a UUID arg; today's MSME deployments share the pending queue across one Owner so the global count is fine. (2) The `RequestedBy` field is `string` (uuid as text) rather than `uuid.UUID` because no caller in the codebase parses UUIDs into `uuid.UUID` values — they shuttle the string through to other RPCs. Adding the dependency for cosmetic typing seemed wasteful; will revisit if T18 needs UUID arithmetic. (3) `Payload []byte` requires every caller to `json.Unmarshal` against the request-type-specific schema. T17's sender will need a small `parseApprovalPayload(requestType, raw)` switch — flagged for that task. (4) Did NOT touch unrelated working-tree drift (`backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `src/components/pembelian/MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, untracked plan docs).
- **Next**: Task 17 of Phase 2 — WA approval sender `backend-go/internal/whatsapp/approval_sender.go`. T17 will format the approval card (TestFormatApprovalMessage_AdjustmentRusak spec'd in the plan) and call `SetWaMessageID` after the WA send returns a message id. T16's helpers are the read substrate the sender lists pending rows from.

## 2026-06-08 — Stock Fraud Phase 2, Task 15: `stock-evidence` storage bucket — DONE

- **Goal**: Create the private Supabase Storage bucket that holds photo evidence for stock adjustments (rusak/hilang per the `chk_evidence_for_loss` CHECK on `stock_adjustments` from T2) and opname variance documentation. Owner previews these files in the Approval Inbox before flipping the gate via PIN modal or WA button (T13/T14). T15 is the substrate; the frontend `StockAdjustmentModal` (later phase task) will upload to `stock-evidence/...` and store the resulting object keys in `evidence_urls TEXT[]` which the T4 `request_adjustment` RPC already accepts.
- **What — migration `supabase/migrations/20260607000021_stock_evidence_bucket.sql`** (NEW, T14 took `…020` so T15 is `…021`): three things, all wrapped in `IF NOT EXISTS` guards so re-runs are no-ops. (1) `INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public) VALUES ('stock-evidence', 'stock-evidence', false) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING` — **private bucket** (public=false) so URLs require a signed token or authenticated session; evidence files may contain notes about loss/damage we do not want public. (2) `CREATE POLICY "authenticated can read stock-evidence" ON storage.objects FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (bucket_id = 'stock-evidence')` — any authenticated user (Owner, Manager, Kasir) may read; the Approval Inbox needs preview access for non-owner roles too (the Manager who submitted needs to see their own past submissions). (3) `CREATE POLICY "authenticated can upload stock-evidence" ON storage.objects FOR INSERT TO authenticated WITH CHECK (bucket_id = 'stock-evidence')` — any authenticated user may upload (the request_adjustment flow uploads BEFORE calling the RPC). Both policies wrapped in `DO $$ … IF NOT EXISTS … END $$` blocks following the pattern from `…012_storage_authenticated_policies.sql` for the payment-proofs idempotency block.
- **Why no UPDATE and no DELETE policy (deliberate omission)**: Evidence files are part of the audit trail once attached to an `approval_request`. The reference pattern in `…012` used a single `FOR ALL` policy that grants UPDATE+DELETE too — that is correct for payment-proofs (uploaded freely as part of the pembelian flow) but WRONG for stock-evidence (which the fraud-prevention spec treats as append-only, mirroring the immutable ledger pattern from Foundational Decision #1). The task description explicitly called this out: "UPDATE/DELETE policies NOT created — evidence files should not be modified after upload". Postgres RLS denies operations that have no matching policy, so authenticated callers receive permission-denied on UPDATE/DELETE against `bucket_id='stock-evidence'`. service_role retains full access for backups/admin maintenance — accepted trade-off per Foundational Decision #1.
- **Why the task description was authoritative over the plan text**: The plan body at line 2184 of `2026-06-07-stock-fraud-phase2.md` proposed (a) sequence number `…012` (which would collide with the existing `…012_storage_authenticated_policies.sql` and `…012_kasir_add_customer_contact.sql` from the 2026-06-04 batch — Phase 2 numbering had already shifted) and (b) included an `UPDATE TO authenticated USING (bucket_id = 'stock-evidence' AND owner = auth.uid())` policy that contradicted the append-only design intent. The task description corrected both: `…021` (cascade from T14=…020) and SELECT+INSERT only. Followed the task description as the source of truth.
- **Verification — live psql against Supabase DB**: `SELECT id, name, public FROM storage.buckets WHERE id='stock-evidence';` returned one row with `public=f`. `SELECT policyname, cmd, roles FROM pg_policies WHERE policyname LIKE '%stock-evidence%';` returned exactly two rows: `authenticated can read stock-evidence` (cmd=SELECT, role=authenticated) and `authenticated can upload stock-evidence` (cmd=INSERT, role=authenticated). Zero UPDATE/DELETE policies as designed.
- **Why no Go test added**: T15's verification is a one-liner against `storage.buckets`; the existing T1-T14 regression suite is unaffected (no schema or RPC change touches `public.*`). Adding a single-row existence assertion would couple the Go test suite to Supabase Storage internals (the `storage.buckets` table is Supabase-managed) for marginal value — the live psql verification above is the durable proof. The frontend upload path will be exercised by the StockAdjustmentModal task later in Phase 2.
- **Test results**: Targeted `go test ./internal/db/... -run TestApproval` suite green (T1-T14 untouched, no T15 test added). `go build ./...` clean. Bucket + 2 policies present, 0 UPDATE/DELETE policies as designed.
- **Concerns**: (1) The `public=false` setting means the frontend MUST request signed URLs (via `supabase.storage.from('stock-evidence').createSignedUrl(path, ttl)`) to render preview thumbnails in the Approval Inbox; downstream UI task will need to surface this. (2) No file-size or MIME-type restriction is set on the bucket — a malicious authenticated user could upload arbitrary large/non-image files. Supabase Storage's bucket-level `file_size_limit` and `allowed_mime_types` are NOT set here; consider tightening to `5 MB` and `image/jpeg, image/png, image/heic` in a follow-up if abuse is observed. (3) Without an UPDATE policy, an authenticated user who uploads the wrong photo cannot replace it — they must upload a new file. This is the intended append-only behavior but worth surfacing in the frontend UX (show "delete & re-upload" as the only remediation path). (4) Did NOT touch the unrelated working-tree drift (`backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `src/components/pembelian/MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, untracked plan docs).
- **Next**: Task 16 of Phase 2 — Go helper `backend-go/internal/db/approvals.go`. T16 adds the typed helpers (`ListPendingApprovalRequests`, `FetchApprovalRequest`, etc.) the Go backend needs to back the WA-webhook handler and the expiry poller wired in T14.

T14 closes the second of the three approval channels (Owner PIN modal from T13, WA buttons here, auto-expiry here too) — every flip routes through the canonical `_transition_approval` helper from `…007`, preserving the SOLE-sanctioned-UPDATE-path invariant.
- **What — migration `supabase/migrations/20260607000020_wa_button_expire.sql`** (NEW file, not appended to `…018` per the plan's stale text): two SECURITY DEFINER functions both owned by postgres (so they retain the REVOKE'd EXECUTE on `_transition_approval`). (1) `decide_via_wa_button(p_approval_request_id BIGINT, p_decision TEXT, p_decided_by_user_id UUID) RETURNS BIGINT` — validates p_decision ∈ ('approved','rejected') with a narrow allow-list, verifies the caller is an Owner via `EXISTS … admin_users WHERE role='Owner'` (raises 'not authorized' otherwise), calls `_transition_approval(.., p_decision::approval_status, p_decided_by_user_id, 'wa_button')`, returns the approval id. GRANT EXECUTE to authenticated (Calista's WA handler runs under authenticated post-JWT). (2) `expire_pending_approvals() RETURNS INT` — FOR loop over `id FROM approval_requests WHERE status='pending' AND expires_at <= now()`, calls `_transition_approval(id, 'expired', NULL, 'auto_expire')` per row, counts successes. Wrapped in `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN CONTINUE` so a racing decision (e.g. Owner PIN approval lands mid-sweep) doesn't poison the rest of the loop. REVOKE EXECUTE from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated; GRANT EXECUTE to service_role only — the poller is a backend concern.
- **What — tests (`backend-go/internal/db/approvals_test.go`, +271 lines)**: Four tests appended after T13's `TestVerifyOwnerPin_WhenLocked_Rejects` with three local helpers (`ensureT14OwnerAdmin`, `ensureT14StaffAdmin`, `seedT14PendingApproval`) — following the T11/T12/T13 inline-helper pattern (no exported `EnsureOwnerUser`). (1) `TestDecideViaWaButton_OwnerApproves` calls the RPC with Owner uuid `…099` + 'approved' → asserts returned id matches, status='approved', decision_channel='wa_button', decided_by=Owner. (2) `TestDecideViaWaButton_NonOwnerRejected` seeds a REAL persisted Staff Admin row (uuid `…088`, role='Staff Admin Toko') — NOT a phantom UUID — so the test verifies the role check fires, not the not-found path. Asserts error contains 'not authorized' and status stays 'pending'. (3) `TestDecideViaWaButton_InvalidDecision` passes 'maybe' as Owner → asserts the validator fires BEFORE the Owner check / `_transition_approval` call; status stays 'pending'. (4) `TestExpirePendingApprovals_FlipsExpiredRows` seeds a pending row, backdates its `expires_at` to `now() - INTERVAL '1 minute'` (the disabled `trg_deny_ar_update` table-level trigger lets service_role UPDATE through for setup), calls expire RPC → asserts return ≥1, row flipped to 'expired' with decision_channel='auto_expire' and decided_by IS NULL. Then seeds a FRESH in-window row, calls expire RPC again → asserts fresh row stays 'pending'. Does NOT assert the second-call return value (other in-flight pending+expired rows in the DB may contribute; we only own the rows we seeded).
- **Why the user task description was authoritative, not the plan text**: The plan referenced modifying `…011_extend_permissions_and_pin.sql`, but `…011` is `stock_opname`, not the PIN migration (which is `…018`); the plan also used `'approve'/'reject'` strings with CASE translation and a direct UPDATE for expire (violating the `_transition_approval` invariant from `…007`). T13's commit `7269b9a` already set the precedent of creating a new `…NNN` migration rather than appending to the plan's named file, and the user's spec corrected the channel-string mismatch + the direct-UPDATE invariant break. Followed the user's explicit instructions: new `…020` migration, `'approved'/'rejected'` to match the enum directly, per-row `_transition_approval` loop in expire, service_role-only grant for expire.
- **Why `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN CONTINUE` in the expire loop**: `_transition_approval` raises if the row is no longer pending (its WHERE clause is `status='pending'`). A racing Owner PIN approval that lands between our `SELECT id` and the helper's UPDATE would re-raise out of the loop, leaving every later expired row unflipped. Catching+continuing is the right trade-off: we lose visibility into the racing flip (counted as not-expired in our return), but we don't silently skip the rest of the sweep. The alternative (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` in the cursor) would block the racing approval, which is worse — the Owner PIN flow is the higher-priority path.
- **Why service_role-only grant for `expire_pending_approvals`**: The Go backend poller is the single sanctioned caller. Client SDKs (anon, authenticated) have no business kicking auto-expiry — the timer is a backend concern. The poller in `backend-go` runs under service_role per the existing connection-string pattern (see `backend-go/.env`'s `SUPABASE_DB_CONNECTION` using the postgres role which inherits service_role's grants). Belt-and-suspenders: REVOKE from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated, GRANT only to service_role.
- **What was NOT done (deliberate)**: did NOT add an exported `db.EnsureOwnerUser` helper — followed T11/T12/T13's inline `ensureT{NN}OwnerAdmin` pattern (no cross-test reuse expected since each task's tests upsert with task-specific email so they don't collide on the `…099` uuid). Did NOT add a `wa_message_id` write path (the column exists on `approval_requests` but T14's spec only flips state; recording the inbound WA message id is a downstream concern for the Calista handler that calls this RPC). Did NOT modify `…018` per the plan's stale text. Did NOT add a row-level lock in the expire SELECT loop (FOR UPDATE) — the EXCEPTION catch handles the race adequately. Did NOT add an index on `expires_at` alone — the existing `idx_ar_status_expires` (status, expires_at) covers the WHERE clause perfectly. Did NOT touch any unrelated working-tree drift (`backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `src/components/pembelian/MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, untracked plan docs).
- **Test results**: All 4 T14 tests pass on the live Supabase DB. Full `internal/db` regression (40+ tests) green: T1-T13 unchanged, T14 added cleanly.
- **Concerns**: (1) The `TestDecideViaWaButton_NonOwnerRejected` test seeds Staff uuid `…088`; if a future task seeds a *different* role on the same uuid it could break this test. Suggest reserving `…088` for non-Owner test fixtures. (2) `expire_pending_approvals` has no rate-limit / batch-size cap. At MSME scale (≪ 100 pending rows expected) this is fine; if the DB ever held tens of thousands of stale-pending rows the single transaction could be long. Mitigation if needed: add a `LIMIT 1000` to the cursor SELECT. (3) The `_transition_approval` call from inside `expire_pending_approvals` runs under SECURITY DEFINER → can flip rows even though authenticated/anon are REVOKE'd from EXECUTE on the helper — this is the intended behavior (the function owner is postgres), but it means a SQL injection in the expire RPC body would have privileged blast radius. The body is hand-written with no dynamic SQL, so no injection surface.
- **Next**: Task 15 of Phase 2 — `stock-evidence` storage bucket. T15 lands the Supabase Storage bucket used by adjustment evidence URLs (the `evidence_urls TEXT[]` column on `stock_adjustments` already populated by the T4 RPC) so the Owner can preview proof photos at decision time.
