## 2026-06-08 — PO Create Page, Task 11: Download PDF button in `PoDetailView` — DONE
- **Goal**: Eleventh task of the PO Create page plan. Hook the Task-10 `generatePoPdf()` Blob-returning library into the live `PoDetailView` modal via a "Download PDF" action button in the header action bar. Button is gated by `po.status !== 'DRAFT'` because PDF should only be issued for finalized POs (DRAFT is internal scratch state — surfacing a download for it would imply legitimacy the PO hasn't earned yet). Click flow: fetch admin name for "Dibuat oleh" line (if `created_by_user_id` set) → generate Blob via `generatePoPdf({...})` → `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` → `window.open(url, '_blank')` to preview in new tab → if popup blocker returns null, fall back to a synthetic `<a download="PO-NUMBER.pdf">` click → revoke the object URL after 60 seconds. Confirm prompt if `company_settings.address` or `.phone` are missing (gives the user a chance to bail and seed Pengaturan first rather than ship a PDF without their contact info).
- **What — imports**: Added `FileText` to the `lucide-react` import (button icon). Added `DbCompanySettings` to the `'../../types'` import (state type). Added `adminUsersService` to the existing `companySettingsService` import from `'../../lib/supabaseClient'` (to resolve `created_by_user_id` → admin name). Added the new line `import { generatePoPdf } from '../../lib/pdf/purchaseOrderPdf'` (the Task-10 library). Five-line delta at the top of the file; merges cleanly with the pre-existing import block.
- **What — state**: Added two new `useState` hooks immediately after the existing `updatingItemId`/`storeName` hooks: `downloadingPdf: boolean` (disables the button + flips its label to "Memproses..." during the async PDF generation, prevents double-click double-render) and `companySettings: DbCompanySettings | null` (the full settings object, passed verbatim to `generatePoPdf`). Refactored the existing `useEffect` that previously called `companySettingsService.fetch().then(s => { if (s?.company_name) setStoreName(s.company_name); })` to ALSO `setCompanySettings(s)` from the same fetch — single network round-trip, both state hooks fed in one shot. Trade-off accepted: minor scope creep beyond the original `setStoreName`-only branch, but the alternative (two separate `useEffect`s firing two identical fetches) would be wasteful.
- **What — `handleDownloadPdf()` async handler**: (a) Early-return if `downloadingPdf` (double-click guard). (b) Hard-fail with a warning toast if `po.supplier` is null/undefined — without supplier data the PDF would render a "KEPADA: undefined" line which is worse than nothing; the toast tells the user to reload. (c) Soft-warn-confirm if `companySettings.address` or `.phone` are missing — `confirm()` modal lets the user choose between bailing (to go fill Pengaturan) and proceeding (PDF will skip those lines per Task 10's null-graceful render). (d) Set `downloadingPdf=true`. (e) Resolve `createdByName`: if `po.created_by_user_id` is set, fetch all admin users via `adminUsersService.fetchAll()` and find by id; default to `'—'` em-dash on any failure (network error, user deleted, dev-mode empty-string id). (f) Call `generatePoPdf({po, supplier: po.supplier, items: po.items ?? [], companySettings, createdByName})` — returns Blob. (g) `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` → `window.open(url, '_blank')` for preview. (h) If `win === null` (popup blocked), synthesize a temporary `<a download={po.po_number + '.pdf'}>` element, append, click, remove — classic popup-blocked fallback pattern. (i) Schedule `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` after 60 seconds via `setTimeout` — gives the new tab time to download/render before the browser frees the Blob; not revoking would leak memory (browser holds onto every unrevoked Blob URL until tab close). (j) Catch any error from generatePoPdf, log to console, toast a warning. (k) `finally` clears `downloadingPdf` regardless of outcome.
- **What — button JSX**: Added a conditional `{po.status !== 'DRAFT' && (<button type="button" onClick={handleDownloadPdf} disabled={downloadingPdf} ...>FileText icon + label</button>)}` inside the existing header action bar `<div className="flex gap-2">`, BEFORE the Print and Close buttons (left-most among the actions — most prominent placement for the most semantically meaningful action). Label flips between "Download PDF" (idle) and "Memproses..." (loading). Styled with indigo theme (`text-indigo-700`, `border-indigo-200`, `bg-indigo-50`, `hover:bg-indigo-100`) to distinguish from the neutral-gray Print button — visually communicates "this is the primary export action; Print is secondary".
- **Why `po.status !== 'DRAFT'` gate, not a more permissive condition**: Task plan spec is explicit — DRAFT POs are internal scratch state; the PDF represents a finalized commitment to the supplier (a legal-ish document). Showing a Download button on DRAFT would invite users to ship a not-yet-finalized PO to a supplier prematurely, which then has to be re-issued if any item is added/removed before ORDERED. ORDERED/RECEIVED/PAID are all legitimate states for a PDF — the supplier-facing document doesn't change its essential content across those status transitions; only the receive-confirmation timestamps do, which is fine since the PDF embeds them as informational metadata, not commitment fields. The boolean gate is the simplest cut that respects the semantic.
- **Why fold `companySettings` state into the existing useEffect rather than create a parallel one**: the existing effect already fetches the settings (for `storeName` display in print header). A second `useEffect` firing the same `companySettingsService.fetch()` would double the network round-trip — wasteful for a static-ish endpoint that returns the same data both times. Single fetch, two `setState` calls is the minimal change; cost is a 2-line edit to the existing effect's `.then` callback, benefit is one network call instead of two. Both `setStoreName` and `setCompanySettings` derive from the same `s` object so they update atomically.
- **Why `window.open(url, '_blank')` first, `<a download>` only as fallback — not the reverse**: opening in a new tab gives the user immediate visual feedback (the PDF renders in-browser, they can scroll and verify before saving), while a synthetic download click jumps straight to "Save As..." which is jarring if the user just wanted to peek at the formatting. Browsers' Save button in the PDF viewer toolbar gives them the download option from the preview tab anyway. But popup blockers (Safari, hardened Chrome profiles, mobile Safari) will block `window.open` from a click handler that crosses an async boundary (`await` for admin fetch) — in those cases the `win === null` check catches it and synthesizes a download link. The fallback is single-action (no preview), but at least the user gets the file. Best of both worlds: preview if browser allows, download if not.
- **Why `setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 60_000)` — not `revokeObjectURL` immediately after `window.open`**: revoking immediately invalidates the URL the new tab is trying to load — the tab gets a "URL not found" error before it can fetch the Blob. 60 seconds is generous; typical browsers finish rendering a small PDF in <1 second, but mobile networks or slow CPUs need a buffer. The trade-off is a 60-second window where the Blob stays in memory; for a single PDF this is fine (PDF Blobs are typically 50-200KB), but if the user spam-clicks 100 PDFs in a minute, that's ~20MB of Blob memory hanging around until the timers fire. Acceptable for the realistic use pattern (1-2 downloads per session); a smarter implementation would track URLs and revoke on tab unload, but that's over-engineering for the actual risk.
- **Why fetch ALL admins via `adminUsersService.fetchAll()` then `.find()` instead of a single targeted lookup**: there's no `adminUsersService.fetchById()` method in the codebase. Adding one is a bigger change (touches supabaseClient.ts which is already huge) and would only be used in one place. The `fetchAll().find()` pattern is wasteful at scale (1000+ admins would be a problem) but the realistic admin count is <20 for any single tenant — the wasted bytes are noise. Future: if the admin count grows, add a `fetchById` and switch. For now, simplicity wins.
- **Why fall back to em-dash `'—'` for createdByName instead of "Unknown" or "Dev User"**: em-dash is the existing convention throughout the app for "no value" — see `formatDate('')` → `'—'`, "Jatuh Tempo" → `'—'` in the same PoDetailView, etc. Using "Unknown" or "—" inconsistently across the UI would be jarring. The PDF's "Dibuat oleh: —" is unambiguous (the line still renders, just with no name) and follows the visual pattern the user already recognizes. Dev-mode users with `created_by_user_id = ''` will get `'—'` (empty string doesn't match any admin id, `.find()` returns undefined), which is the correct behavior — the PDF wasn't created by a real admin user.
- **Why hard-fail (warning toast + early return) on missing `po.supplier` but soft-warn-confirm on missing `companySettings.address/phone`**: supplier is an existential prerequisite — without it the PDF's KEPADA section would render "KEPADA: undefined undefined", which is visibly broken. Reload-the-page is the realistic fix (the supplier should always be JOIN'd on the PO query). Company address/phone, in contrast, are presentational — the PDF still renders fine without them (Task 10's null-graceful render falls back to a name-only company line), but the supplier won't know how to contact the buyer back. The user might legitimately want to ship a PDF without those (e.g., they're sending it via WA where contact info is implicit), so a confirm() lets them proceed. Different severity, different UX.
- **Why indigo button color (not emerald like the rest of the brand or amber like the warning palette)**: emerald is reserved for the brand mark + primary positive actions (Simpan, Bayar, etc.); using it for "Download PDF" would dilute the brand-action visual signal. Amber is for warnings and pending states (PPN highlight, Pending Return) — wrong semantic. Gray (like the Print button) would make the Download button visually indistinguishable from Print, but PDF download IS a more deliberate action than Print (it generates a new artifact rather than rendering the current view). Indigo is a tertiary "export/share" color that's distinct from both the brand and the warning palette, used elsewhere in the app for the invoice/payment-proof links — visual consistency with "external document export" pattern.
- **Lint verification — zero NEW errors, baseline 12 → 12**: `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → 12 errors total, all pre-existing: App.tsx StockItem mismatch ×2, PurchaseOrderFormPage.tsx `key` prop on ItemRowProps (Task 8 carry-over), SalesInboxScreen.tsx `key` prop, Sidebar.tsx `'auth'` dead comparison, send-admin-invite Deno imports ×7. ZERO errors mention `src/components/pembelian/PoDetailView.tsx` — the new imports, state hooks, and JSX compile clean against existing types. The handler's `try { ... } catch (e: any)` uses the same pattern as `handleDamageStatusChange` already in the file.
- **What was NOT done (deliberate)**: did NOT add a "preview PDF in iframe" affordance — `window.open` already opens the PDF in a new tab which gives an effective preview; an iframe overlay would be redundant UX. Did NOT add a "Send to WA" or "Email supplier" button on top of the Blob — out of scope for Task 11 (those are future Tasks if/when they're prioritized). Did NOT replace the existing browser-native `confirm()` with a custom modal for the address/phone warning — the existing app uses native `confirm()` for destructive/decision actions (see `handleDelete` in OrdersTab), so we're matching convention. Did NOT add a server-side PDF generation path — jsPDF runs client-side only; this is fine since the user is the one initiating the download. Did NOT pre-fetch `adminUsers` on mount alongside `companySettings` — the admin fetch only fires on PDF download click, which is rare; pre-fetching would waste bandwidth on users who never download. Did NOT touch `PoDetailView`'s existing Print button — that's the browser-native print path which uses the inline DOM, totally orthogonal to the PDF library path. Did NOT touch the other modified-but-uncommitted working-tree files (`.gitignore`, `backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, `approvals_test.go`, untracked plan/spec/migration files) — pre-existing user work, out-of-scope per the named-files-only rule.
- **Self-review checklist**: (a) Single named file modified: `src/components/pembelian/PoDetailView.tsx`. (b) Imports merged correctly: `FileText` added to lucide-react, `DbCompanySettings` added to types, `adminUsersService` added to supabaseClient, new `generatePoPdf` import. (c) Two new `useState` hooks (`downloadingPdf`, `companySettings`) added after existing hooks. (d) Existing useEffect now sets BOTH `setStoreName` (preserved) AND `setCompanySettings` (new) — single fetch round-trip. (e) `handleDownloadPdf()` async handler matches the plan spec verbatim: double-click guard → supplier hard-fail → company info soft-warn-confirm → admin fetch with em-dash fallback → generatePoPdf call with 5 args → URL.createObjectURL → window.open with popup-blocked fallback → 60s revoke timer → catch+console+toast → finally clears downloadingPdf. (f) Button rendered conditionally on `po.status !== 'DRAFT'`, placed left of Print in the existing header action bar. (g) Button disabled during downloadingPdf, label flips to "Memproses...". (h) Indigo styling matches the plan spec exactly. (i) Lint = 12 errors = exact baseline, zero NEW errors. (j) Single clean commit, only the one named file in the diff.
- **Concerns**: (1) `fetchAll().find()` pattern is wasteful if admin count grows past ~50 — a per-id `fetchById` would be cleaner. Acceptable for current realistic tenant size (<20 admins). (2) 60-second URL revoke timer leaks Blob memory if the user closes the tab early or spam-downloads — mobile Safari is particularly memory-constrained. Realistic impact is negligible (typical PDF Blob is <200KB, one or two downloads per session) but visible under pathological usage. (3) The popup-blocked fallback uses `<a download>` which always saves to the default downloads folder — no preview, no opportunity for the user to verify the PDF before keeping it. Acceptable as fallback; the primary path (window.open) gives the preview. (4) `companySettings` is fetched on every mount of `PoDetailView` (each PO modal open) — would be smarter to lift this to a higher-level context or a memoized hook, but `PoDetailView` is opened relatively rarely and the fetch is small, so the redundant call is noise not concern. (5) The `confirm()` for missing company info is browser-native — accessibility-wise this is fine on desktop, but mobile Safari and some Android browsers render `confirm()` modally in a way that varies. Acceptable; matches the existing app's pattern.
- **Files**: `src/components/pembelian/PoDetailView.tsx` (modified, +71/-4), `progress.md` (this entry).

- **Next**: Task 12 of the PO Create page plan — add "Tgl Diterima" column + "Telat" badge to `OrdersTab` for expected-receive-date tracking.

## 2026-06-08 — PO Create Page, Task 10: `purchaseOrderPdf.ts` — PDF rendering library — DONE
- **Goal**: Tenth task of the PO Create page plan. Land the pure-function `generatePoPdf({po, supplier, items, companySettings, createdByName}) → Blob` library that renders a branded A4 portrait PDF of a Purchase Order. No React, no Supabase, no IO — single export that takes data and returns bytes. Task 11 will hook this Blob to a "Download PDF" button in `PoDetailView` via the standard `URL.createObjectURL → <a download>` dance. Isolating the PDF logic in `src/lib/pdf/` keeps the printable representation independent of any specific UI surface — same function can drive the Detail view's download button, a future "email to supplier" workflow, a batch-print queue, etc.
- **What — directory + file**: Created new directory `src/lib/pdf/` (alongside existing `src/lib/` files `pembelianService.ts`, `salesEntries.ts`, `supabaseClient.ts`). The dedicated `pdf/` sub-namespace gives room for future PDF generators (invoices, receipts, return memos, kasir shift reports) without polluting `src/lib/` root. Created `src/lib/pdf/purchaseOrderPdf.ts` (243 lines, single default-export `generatePoPdf`). Verbatim implementation from the plan spec — no adaptations, no improvements, no concerns.
- **What — PDF structure**: A4 portrait via `new jsPDF({ unit: 'pt', format: 'a4' })`. Five visual sections from top to bottom: (1) Header — 36×36pt emerald (`#2d8a4e`) rounded brand box with a manually-drawn lightning-bolt approximation (two white `doc.triangle()` calls forming a Zap shape), company name (16pt bold) + `MSME ERP SUITE` tagline (7pt bold emerald) + optional address/phone/email lines from `companySettings`, with `PURCHASE ORDER` (18pt bold) + `po_number` (11pt courier bold) right-aligned. (2) Header divider — 1.5pt dark horizontal line full-width. (3) Two-column info block — left "KEPADA" (supplier name + optional Kontak/HP-WA + Term line), right "DETAIL PO" (Tgl Pesan / Diterima paling lambat / Dibuat oleh) as a manually-drawn label-value table with amber-highlighted row for non-null `expected_receive_date`. (4) Items table via `jspdf-autotable` — 6 columns (No / SKU / Nama Produk / Qty / Harga / Subtotal), plain theme, monospaced courier font on the SKU column for visual scan, light gray header fill. (5) Totals — right-aligned Subtotal + optional PPN row (when `po.tax_rate > 0`) + bold-border TOTAL row using `formatRupiah()` helper. (6) Optional Notes section (when `po.notes`) with light divider + multi-line text wrap via `doc.splitTextToSize`. (7) Footer T&C — light gray divider + centered Indonesian "Barang yang dikirim wajib sesuai spesifikasi PO. Konfirmasi penerimaan via WA dalam 1×24 jam." 8pt muted text.
- **Why a pure Blob-returning function rather than auto-trigger-download or React-bound**: separation of concerns. The PDF rendering knows nothing about navigation, click handlers, browser APIs (`URL.createObjectURL`), filename conventions, or React state. The caller controls all of that. Same `generatePoPdf` can drive (a) a click-to-download button (Task 11's actual use case in `PoDetailView`), (b) a server-side PDF generation if we ever move this to a Cloud Function, (c) an embedded preview via iframe + blob URL, (d) batch email to multiple suppliers. By returning a `Blob`, we get a primitive the caller can do anything with. Pure function = testable; an integration test could call `generatePoPdf(fixtureData)` and assert the Blob's size or MIME type without spinning up a DOM.
- **Why `companySettings: DbCompanySettings | null` (nullable) but `supplier: DbSupplier` (required)**: a Purchase Order without a supplier is conceptually impossible — supplier_id is `NOT NULL` on the DB column. But `company_settings` is a single config row that may not be seeded in fresh installs (e.g., during dev or a brand-new tenant). The function handles `null` gracefully — falls back to a hardcoded `'Garindo Jaya Panel'` company name and skips the address/phone/email lines entirely. The caller (Task 11) loads `company_settings` once and passes whatever it gets, even if that's null. No null-check at the call site needed.
- **Why `createdByName: string` rather than `createdByUserId: string` + DB lookup**: the function should not know how to query Supabase. Forcing the caller to resolve the user id → name mapping before calling `generatePoPdf` keeps this library zero-IO. Task 11 will resolve via the existing user-lookup pattern (probably via `currentUser.full_name` if the PO was created by the current user, or a fetch from `admin_users` if not). Side benefit: dev-mode users (no real Supabase user, `created_by_user_id = null`) can pass any string ("Dev User", "Unknown") and the PDF still renders.
- **Why drawing the Zap lightning bolt with two `doc.triangle()` calls instead of an embedded SVG/PNG**: jsPDF has no native SVG-path renderer (the `svg2pdf.js` plugin exists but adds 100KB+ of dependency for a single icon). An embedded PNG would force a base64-encoded asset (50-100KB inlined into every PDF). Two filled triangles approximate the Zap shape with zero additional dependencies and zero asset bytes. The result is a stylized lightning bolt that reads correctly at the small 36pt size — fidelity isn't critical for a brand glyph at this resolution. Future polish (using `addImage()` with a base64 PNG of the actual Zap SVG) is a one-line change if visual fidelity matters more than dependency footprint.
- **Why `'helvetica'` for body and `'courier'` for SKU/po_number — no Indonesian-Latin font issues**: jsPDF ships with the 14 PDF standard fonts (Helvetica, Times, Courier, Symbol, ZapfDingbats) and those handle Latin-1 (Indonesian uses the same alphabet, no diacritics beyond the rare ç or é which Latin-1 covers). No font-loading dance, no `vfs_fonts.js` boilerplate, no Unicode subsetting needed. Courier mono on the SKU column is a deliberate visual signal — SKUs are technical identifiers (`STK-0123-ABC`), monospace makes them scan-friendly. The PO number gets the same treatment in the header.
- **Why amber highlight on the "Diterima paling lambat" row only when `expected_receive_date` is set**: the amber row visually anchors the most operationally-important date on the PO — the deadline the supplier promised. When that date is null (legacy POs or DRAFT without a target), no highlight makes sense — there's no commitment to flag. The conditional `highlight: !!po.expected_receive_date` cleanly toggles between the highlighted-bold-amber and the muted-normal style for the row, using the same render loop. Amber (`#fef3c7` bg, `#92400e` text) is the Tailwind warning palette — matches the "Telat" badge that Task 12 will add to OrdersTab when expected date has passed.
- **Why `(doc as any).lastAutoTable.finalY` cast — jspdf-autotable's TS types are upstream-broken**: `jspdf-autotable` extends the jsPDF instance with a `lastAutoTable` property at runtime, but its TypeScript types don't augment the `jsPDF` type interface. The official fix from the maintainer is to either declare a module augmentation in a `.d.ts` file or use the `any` cast at the call site. Single-use `any` cast is the lowest-friction fix — no new declaration file, no global type pollution. Same pattern is used in many jspdf-autotable production codebases. Future-proof: if jspdf-autotable v4+ ships with proper TS types, the cast can be dropped without affecting behavior.
- **Why `'#fef3c7'`/`'#92400e'`/`'#e5e7eb'`/`'#d1d5db'`/`'#f3f4f6'` hardcoded hex strings rather than imported palette constants**: this file is the rendering layer's only consumer of those colors — they don't appear elsewhere in the lib/ tree. Centralizing into a `palette.ts` would be premature abstraction for one consumer. The colors match the Tailwind palette (`amber-100`/`amber-800`/`gray-200`/`gray-300`/`gray-100`) the rest of the UI uses, but jsPDF doesn't speak Tailwind class names — it speaks RGB or hex. Hardcoding is the lowest-friction path; if a second PDF generator joins the `pdf/` namespace and wants the same palette, that's the right time to extract.
- **Why `formatRupiah` and `formatDateID` are file-local helpers, not imports from a shared lib**: looked for existing helpers — `src/lib/` has no money-formatting utility (the rest of the app uses inline `.toLocaleString('id-ID')`), and there's no date-formatting helper for Indonesian month names. Creating a shared helper for two two-line functions used in one place would be over-engineering. If a third consumer of the same format pattern emerges, that's the trigger to extract. Both functions are pure, deterministic, and trivially testable in-line.
- **Lint verification — zero NEW errors, baseline 12 → 12**: `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → 12 errors total. All 12 are pre-existing: App.tsx StockItem mismatch ×2, PurchaseOrderFormPage.tsx `key` prop on ItemRowProps (Task 8's accepted error), SalesInboxScreen.tsx `key` prop, Sidebar.tsx `'auth'` dead comparison, send-admin-invite Deno imports ×7. ZERO errors mention `src/lib/pdf/purchaseOrderPdf.ts` — the new file compiles clean against the existing types. The `(doc as any).lastAutoTable.finalY` cast handles the one known TS quirk of `jspdf-autotable`. Standalone `npx tsc --noEmit --strict` on just the new file (with relaxed module config) produced zero output — confirms clean compile in isolation too.
- **What was NOT done (deliberate)**: did NOT wire the function into `PoDetailView` or add a "Download PDF" button — that's Task 11's explicit scope. Did NOT add a server-side render mode — jsPDF runs in the browser only, and we have no PDF generation backend right now. Did NOT add a preview-in-iframe affordance — Task 11 may add it on top via `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` but it's not this task's concern. Did NOT add `<img>` embedding for a real company logo — the emerald Zap box is the brand mark for now, and adding logo support means adding an `image_url` column to `company_settings` + a CORS-safe image fetch + base64 conversion — out of scope. Did NOT add page-break handling for very long PO line items (40+ rows would overflow the single page) — jspdf-autotable's `pageBreak: 'auto'` is the default but the totals section uses absolute `lastAutoTable.finalY + 12` which assumes single-page. Fine for typical POs (5-15 lines); 40-line POs would need a multi-page totals tweak in a follow-up. Did NOT add filename suggestion (the caller's `<a download="PO-NUMBER.pdf">` will set that). Did NOT touch any other files — single-file commit. Did NOT touch the modified-but-uncommitted working-tree files (`.gitignore`, `backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, untracked plan/spec/migration files) — pre-existing user work, out-of-scope per the named-files-only rule.

## 2026-06-08 — PO Create Page, Task 9: ManajemenGudangScreen + sidebar — DONE (b6e1b88)
- **Goal**: Integrate Task 8's `PurchaseOrderFormPage` orchestrator into the production app flow by wiring it as a sub-view of `PembelianScreen` (replacing the modal-based `PurchaseOrderModal` experience) and removing the now-obsolete modal file from the tree. This is the integration step that finally lets a user actually USE the new full-page create/edit PO flow end-to-end. State for "are we creating/editing/listing" is hoisted from the `OrdersTab` sub-component up to `PembelianScreen` so the sub-view can render in the same scroll region as the list (replacing it, not stacked above as a modal). Also threads `currentUser.id` and `currentUser.permissions` from `App.tsx` down through `PembelianScreen` into the form page — required for the audit columns (`created_by`/`updated_by`) and the permission gate (`can_create_po`/`can_edit_po`) that Tasks 1 and 8 wired up.
- **What — `PembelianScreen.tsx`**: Removed `PurchaseOrderModal` import. Added `PurchaseOrderFormPage` import. Added `PermissionSet` import. Added two new props on `PembelianScreenProps` — `currentUserId?: string` and `currentUserPermissions?: PermissionSet`. Added discriminated union type `ViewMode = { kind: 'list' } | { kind: 'create' } | { kind: 'edit'; po: DbPurchaseOrder }` and `useState<ViewMode>({ kind: 'list' })`. Wrapped the main render body (summary cards + tabs + OrdersTab/SuppliersTab) in a ternary: when `viewMode.kind !== 'list'`, render `<PurchaseOrderFormPage>` with all 10 props wired (po, suppliers, orders, stockList, currentUserId, currentUserPermissions, onBack, onSaved, onSupplierAdded, showToast); otherwise render the original list UI. `onSaved` keeps the form open after a draft save (lets the user keep editing) but pops back to the list after a Simpan & Pesan (status transitions to ORDERED). `onSupplierAdded` triggers `reload()` so the supplier list refreshes after an inline supplier-create. Hoisted state OUT of `OrdersTab` — removed the two local `useState` hooks (`showCreateModal`, `editPo`) and added `onCreate` + `onEdit` callbacks to `OrdersTabProps`. Wired "Buat PO Baru" button to `onCreate` and the per-row Edit button to `onEdit(po)`. Deleted the entire `(showCreateModal || editPo) && <PurchaseOrderModal>` conditional render block from the end of `OrdersTab`. The other 4 conditional renders (ReceiveGoodsModal, PoDetailView, MarkAsPaidModal, ReceiveReplacementModal) stay — they're orthogonal to the create/edit flow.
- **What — `src/components/pembelian/PurchaseOrderModal.tsx`**: Deleted via `git rm` (staged as `D`). 256 lines removed from the tree. Last reference (the import in PembelianScreen.tsx) was already cut in the same commit, so the build stays green. `grep -rn "PurchaseOrderModal" src/` returned only the three references that the commit removes — no orphan callsites elsewhere in the codebase.
- **What — `App.tsx`**: Added `id: string` to the `currentUser` `useState` shape. Threaded `id: user.id` into the Supabase session-restore branch (line 74). Added `currentUserId={currentUser?.id}` + `currentUserPermissions={currentUser?.permissions}` to the `<PembelianScreen>` call in `renderPage()`. Updated `handleLoginSuccess` param type to include `id: string`.
- **What — `AuthScreen.tsx` (extra cascade not in the task brief but required by TS)**: The `onLoginSuccess` prop type had to grow `id: string` too — otherwise `handleLoginSuccess` couldn't type-check against its caller. Updated the `AuthScreenProps` interface. Three callsites needed `id` added: (a) `devBypass` uses `id: ''` (no real Supabase user in dev mode), (b) sign-in `verifyOtp` success uses `id: user.id` (real user available from the response), (c) sign-up uses `id: data.user?.id ?? ''` (defensive — `data.user` is technically optional in the supabase-js response type). Real IDs preferred over empty strings where the runtime value exists, since the whole point of plumbing `id` is to power audit + permissions; an empty string would silently break those features for that user.
- **Why hoist `showCreateModal`/`editPo` state out of OrdersTab — not just gate the FormPage render with a sibling state**: the FormPage needs to render in the SAME scroll region as the list (replacing it visually), not stacked above it as a modal. The list is rendered inside `<div className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto px-6 py-5 space-y-5">`, which is owned by `PembelianScreen` (parent), not `OrdersTab` (child). To swap that div's content between "list" and "form page", the discriminator (`viewMode`) must live in the parent. Pulling state up is the React-idiomatic move; the alternative (a portal or a context) would be overkill for this single integration point. The cost: `OrdersTab` now takes two new callback props (`onCreate`, `onEdit`) — fine, since they're domain-meaningful action verbs, not state-leak.
- **Why `onSaved(status)` with two different behaviors (stay vs back)**: a user clicking "Simpan Draft" wants to keep iterating — pricing a few more lines, double-checking discount totals, etc. Popping back to the list every time they save a draft would be punishing. A user clicking "Simpan & Pesan" is done — the PO is ORDERED, no more editing, time to see it in the list with the new Dipesan badge and Terima action. So `onSaved` takes the resulting status and the parent decides: ORDERED → back to list, DRAFT → stay on page. The form page itself doesn't know about the parent's navigation model; it just reports the status. Clean separation.
- **Why threading `currentUserPermissions` through PembelianScreen (a Pembelian-scoped screen) rather than reading from a context**: there's no `UserContext` in this codebase — `currentUser` lives in `App.tsx`'s `useState` and is drilled down to every screen as a prop. Following the existing convention (see `UserManagementScreen`, `OrderHistoryScreen`, `KasirScreen` — all take `currentUser` as a prop) keeps the wiring uniform. The cost is one extra prop on PembelianScreen and a `?.` chain on the value; the benefit is a uniform prop-drilling pattern that's easy to grep for and easy to refactor to a context later if scale demands.
- **Why `currentUserId?: string` (optional) and `currentUserPermissions?: PermissionSet` (optional) rather than required**: when `currentUser` is null (during the brief window between `auth` state and the dashboard mount), `currentUser?.id` is `undefined`. Making the props required would force a non-null assertion at the call site (`currentUser!.id`) — uglier and more brittle. The downstream FormPage handles `undefined` permissions gracefully (uses `!== false` so undefined ALLOWS, per Task 8's convention). The audit columns (`created_by`/`updated_by`) accept `null` in the DB. So optional-with-fallback is the lowest-friction path.

## 2026-06-08 — Stock Fraud Phase 2, Task 13: `verify_owner_pin` RPC — bcrypt + per-Owner lockout — DONE
- **Goal**: Ship the SQL hop that turns "Owner enters PIN in the Approval Modal" into a flipped `approval_requests.status='approved'`. SECURITY DEFINER RPC `public.verify_owner_pin(p_approval_id BIGINT, p_pin TEXT) RETURNS BOOLEAN` that (1) selects the canonical Owner row (`role='Owner' ORDER BY id LIMIT 1`) FOR UPDATE so the lockout counter on that row is the per-org chokepoint per Foundational Decision #6, (2) refuses with `RAISE EXCEPTION 'Owner PIN is locked until %'` if `pin_locked_until > now()` (even a correct PIN cannot bypass — only time can), (3) refuses with `'Owner PIN not configured'` if `approval_pin_hash IS NULL`, (4) locks the target `approval_requests` row and refuses if not `pending`, (5) bcrypt-compares `crypt(p_pin, hash) = hash` — on match resets `pin_failed_count=0, pin_locked_until=NULL` and calls `_transition_approval(.., 'approved', owner_id, 'owner_pin')` returning TRUE; on mismatch increments the counter and arms the 1-hour lockout once the post-increment count reaches 5, returning FALSE without raising. UI distinguishes "wrong PIN" (FALSE) from "locked" (raised exception) cleanly.
- **What — Migration (`supabase/migrations/20260607000019_verify_owner_pin.sql`)**: filename uses `…019` because T12 burned `…018`. `LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER` with `SET search_path = public, extensions` — pgcrypto's `crypt()` / `gen_salt()` live in the `extensions` schema on Supabase, and the function body's unqualified `crypt(...)` call must resolve there; `public` is listed first so app-owned objects still shadow any extension-name collisions. Function owned by postgres so it bypasses the column-level REVOKE on `admin_users.approval_pin_hash` / `pin_failed_count` / `pin_locked_until`. `GRANT EXECUTE … TO authenticated` so SDK callers from the in-app modal can invoke it directly. Uses `_transition_approval` (Phase 2 T1's helper) as the SOLE write path to `approval_requests` — same canonical pattern as T4 (commit_approved_adjustment) and T8 (commit_opname). The wrong-PIN branch preserves the previously-set `pin_locked_until` via `CASE WHEN … ELSE pin_locked_until END` so a stale lock doesn't get wiped by a sub-5 failure burst.
- **What — Tests (`backend-go/internal/db/approvals_test.go`, +192 lines)**: Three tests appended after T12's `TestAdminUsers_PgcryptoAvailable`. Local helpers `ensureT13OwnerWithPin` (upserts `…099` Owner with `crypt('123456', gen_salt('bf'))` PIN hash + resets counter/lock) and `seedT13PendingApproval` (inserts a bare `approval_requests` row of type `adjustment` — skipping `request_adjustment` to avoid stock/state dependencies the RPC under test doesn't care about). (1) `TestVerifyOwnerPin_Success` asserts the RPC returns TRUE for the correct PIN, the approval flips to `approved` with `decision_channel='owner_pin'`, and `pin_failed_count` is reset to 0. (2) `TestVerifyOwnerPin_WrongPin_IncrementsOwnerCounter` fires 5 wrong-PIN calls in a row, then asserts `pin_failed_count >= 5`, `pin_locked_until IS NOT NULL`, and the approval is still `pending` — wrong PIN never advances the gate. (3) `TestVerifyOwnerPin_WhenLocked_Rejects` force-locks the Owner (`pin_locked_until = now() + 1 hour`) and then calls with the CORRECT PIN — must raise an error containing `"locked"`, approval still pending. The third test resets the lock on teardown so the lockout doesn't bleed into subsequent T14+ tests against the same Owner row.
- **Why pin Owner via `ORDER BY id LIMIT 1` + seed `…099`**: the production DB has 4 Owner rows (`…099` + 3 real UUIDs). All-zeros prefix sorts first lexicographically so `…099` is deterministically the row the RPC picks — confirmed via `SELECT id FROM admin_users WHERE role='Owner' ORDER BY id LIMIT 1`. This pins the test seed to the same row the RPC will touch. Multi-Owner orgs accept the trade-off that the lockout becomes org-wide rather than per-Owner; the alternative (loop through all Owners and check each hash) leaks "which Owner approved" timing info via the per-row crypt cost.
- **Why `extensions` on search_path**: first apply failed at runtime with `function crypt(text, text) does not exist` — `SET search_path = public` alone hides pgcrypto. Test `TestAdminUsers_PgcryptoAvailable` passed because the session-level search_path includes extensions, masking the issue at the migration's SQL surface. Lesson for future SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that call pgcrypto: pin both `public` and `extensions`.
- **Why wrong PIN returns FALSE, locked raises EXCEPTION**: two failure modes deserve two signals. Wrong PIN is a user-error UX event (clear the field, count down attempts in the UI); locked is an authorization wall (show the unlock-time toast, gray out the modal). Raising on wrong PIN would force the UI to parse error strings; returning FALSE on locked would force the UI to read `pin_locked_until` separately. The chosen split lets the SDK call await a BOOLEAN with try/catch and route both branches cleanly.
- **What was NOT done (deliberate)**: did NOT implement the 10-minute consecutive-failures window — locks after 5 cumulative failures regardless of timing; tightening to "5 within 10 minutes" requires either an extra `pin_first_fail_at` column or a windowed query and adds little fraud-prevention value for MSME scale. Did NOT export a `db.EnsureOwnerUser` helper — followed T11/T12's `ensureT11OwnerAdmin` inline-helper pattern instead. Did NOT modify the legacy `…011` migration the plan text suggested — `…011` is `stock_opname` and is already committed; T13 ships its own `…019` migration. Did NOT add a CHECK constraint on `pin_failed_count >= 0` — the RPC is the only writer and won't decrement past 0. Did NOT add an index on `pin_locked_until` — lookup is single-row by id, full-scan-free. Did NOT touch any unrelated working-tree drift (`backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `src/components/pembelian/MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, `progress.md` pre-existing edits, untracked plan docs).
- **Test plan executed**: `cd backend-go && go test ./internal/db/ -run 'TestVerifyOwnerPin' -count=1 -v` → 3 PASS in 6.86s. Full regression `cd backend-go && go test ./internal/db/ -count=1 -p 1 -parallel 1` → ALL PASS in 93.5s.
- **Concerns**: (1) The `TestVerifyOwnerPin_WhenLocked_Rejects` cleanup resets `pin_failed_count=0, pin_locked_until=NULL` at end-of-test — but if the test panics before reaching the cleanup line (no `defer` wrapper), the next test that calls the RPC on the same `…099` Owner row will hit a locked state. Mitigation: `ensureT13OwnerWithPin` resets state at the *start* of each T13 test, so the trio is idempotent — but any *T14+* test that calls `verify_owner_pin` against `…099` without first calling `ensureT13OwnerWithPin` could observe a leaked lock. Surfacing here so T14's author sees it. (2) `_transition_approval`'s `p_decided_by` UUID is the Owner's `admin_users.id`, which matches the column type — but the same UUID may not exist in `auth.users` if Supabase Auth isn't seeded for that Owner; the FK from `approval_requests.decided_by` is to `admin_users.id` (not `auth.users`), so this is safe in practice. (3) The session-level pgcrypto availability in `TestAdminUsers_PgcryptoAvailable` masked the function-level search_path miss on first apply — added a postmortem note above; future SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that call pgcrypto must include `extensions` on their pinned search_path.
- **Next**: Task 14 of Phase 2 — `decide_via_wa_button` + `expire_pending_approvals` RPCs. T14 adds the WhatsApp button-decision path (Owner approves via Calista's outbound buttons instead of the in-app PIN modal) and the 24-hour auto-expiry sweeper.

## 2026-06-08 — Stock Fraud Phase 2, Task 12: `admin_users` PIN columns + extended permissions JSONB + pgcrypto — DONE
- **Goal**: Land the storage substrate for Phase 2's Owner-PIN approval path (T13's `verify_owner_pin` RPC) and the 19 action-level permission keys from spec Foundational Decision #5. Three pieces in one migration: (1) `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto` for bcrypt PIN hashing (`crypt()`, `gen_salt('bf')`); (2) three new PIN-state columns on `public.admin_users` (`approval_pin_hash TEXT`, `pin_failed_count INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `pin_locked_until TIMESTAMPTZ`); (3) backfill `permissions` JSONB on every existing admin_users row with the 19 action keys per role-default matrix, using the `||` merge operator so existing sidebar keys (`dashboard`, `kasir`, `userManagement`, …) are preserved untouched. One JSONB column, one source of truth, one UI section — no parallel `action_permissions` column.
- **What — Migration (`supabase/migrations/20260607000018_extend_permissions_and_pin.sql`)**: filename uses `…018` because Phase 2 already burned `…011` (stock_opname) through `…017` (revoke_stocks_writes from T11). pgcrypto extension first; then ALTER TABLE adds the three PIN columns IF NOT EXISTS (idempotent against partial re-apply); then four UPDATE statements seed action permissions per role. Owner gets ALL 19 keys true (locked-on for `can_approve_*`, `can_commit_opname`, `can_view_pengawasan` at the UI layer; backend gate still reads true here). Staff Admin Toko + Staff Admin (legacy label) get 10 request-only keys (`can_request_adjustment`, `can_witness_opname`, `can_request_price_change`, `can_witness_po_receipt`, `can_open_kasir_shift`, three `can_request_kasir_*`, `can_initiate_transfer`, `can_receive_transfer`). Supervisor Gudang gets 7 keys covering opname ownership + adjustment requests + price-change requests + transfers + PO receipt witness. Finance Manager gets 2 keys (`can_witness_opname` for independent count checks + `can_request_price_change`). All `can_approve_*` and `can_commit_opname` and `can_view_pengawasan` default-false for every non-Owner role.
- **What — Tests (`backend-go/internal/db/approvals_test.go`, +136 lines)**: Three new tests append cleanly after T11's `TestSeedStockRow_ExistingSKU_Fails`. (1) `TestAdminUsers_PinColumnsExist` queries `information_schema.columns` for the three PIN columns on `public.admin_users` and asserts all three are present. (2) `TestAdminUsers_OwnerHasAllActionPermissions` seeds a deterministic Owner row with id `…099`, replays the migration's exact `permissions = permissions || jsonb_build_object(...)` merge against that specific row (so the assertion is independent of pre-migration Owner state in CI / fresh DBs), then asserts three representative keys are true: `can_approve_adjustment` (Owner-locked), `can_view_pengawasan` (Phase 4 forward-looking), `can_approve_kasir_refund` (Phase 3b kasir gate). (3) `TestAdminUsers_PgcryptoAvailable` calls `SELECT crypt('test', gen_salt('bf'))` and asserts the output starts with `$2` (the bcrypt prefix family — `$2a$`, `$2b$`, etc.) — proves both `crypt()` and `gen_salt()` are wired correctly so T13's verify path will compile.
- **Why seed action keys via `||` merge instead of replacing the JSONB**: the existing `admin_users.permissions` JSONB carries 11 sidebar keys (`dashboard`, `kasir`, `userManagement`, etc.) that drive the left-nav rendering. Replacing the JSONB would wipe those sidebar settings on every existing admin user — hours of per-user manual fix-up. The `||` operator merges right-side keys into the existing object; right-side wins on conflict, and the 19 action keys don't collide with any of the 11 sidebar keys (different naming convention: `can_*` vs. camelCase). One column, one source of truth, two semantic sections rendered as two UI groups ("Akses Menu" / "Akses Aksi") in User Management.
- **Why test 2 seeds + merges on its own Owner row, not asserting against pre-existing Owner**: the migration's `UPDATE … WHERE role='Owner'` only touches rows that existed at migration time. On a fresh CI DB with zero Owner rows, the test would query a row that doesn't exist and fail. On a dev DB where the seed Owner was inserted post-migration, the action keys would never have been merged in. The test sidesteps both edge cases by inserting its own Owner row and replaying the exact merge logic — which proves the migration's seeding pattern is sound (the SQL works) AND gives a deterministic row to assert against. The trade-off: test 2 doesn't verify the migration's UPDATE actually ran against pre-existing Owners — only that the merge pattern itself works. Acceptable: the SQL is small enough to read-and-confirm by eye, and `UPDATE` row count (4 Owner rows in this run) was visible at migration-apply time as a sanity check.
- **Why include forward-looking phase-3/4 keys in T12, not just Phase 2 keys**: the plan body lists only 8 Phase 2 keys (the seven from the role matrix table + `can_view_pengawasan`). The task brief (more recent override) says all 19 keys per Foundational Decision #5. Chose to seed all 19 now because (a) it avoids a future migration `…0xx_seed_phase3_permissions.sql` that just repeats the same `||` pattern with different keys; (b) the keys cost zero storage when default-false; (c) the TypeScript `PermissionSet` extension on the same commit declares them all optional, so the front-end and back-end stay in lockstep. Owner gets all 19 true; other roles get their phase-specific defaults true now even though the corresponding RPCs (e.g., `request_kasir_void`) don't exist yet — when those land in Phase 3b/3d, the gate already exists for the right roles.
- **TypeScript — `src/types.ts` PermissionSet extended with 19 optional action keys + ALL_PERMISSIONS const**: user's prior commit `b48fbf9` had added `can_create_po?` and `can_edit_po?` as the first two optional keys (Phase 1 PO module). This task adds the remaining 19 (Phase 2 → Phase 4) all as optional `boolean | undefined` since the JSONB column doesn't guarantee any specific key is present on legacy rows. Order matches spec Foundational Decision #5 verbatim. `ALL_PERMISSIONS` const (used as the all-true default for new Owner users in the User Management create form) gets all 19 keys set to `true` — so creating a new Owner via the UI gets the full action-key grant, matching the migration's Owner seed.
- **TS typecheck baseline preserved — 17 errors before, 16 after (one fewer, not more)**: `npx tsc --noEmit` before my change: 17 errors. After: 16 errors. The drop is a one-line shift in the existing error pile, not a regression — verified by grepping the output for any error mentioning `PermissionSet`, `types.ts`, or `ALL_PERMISSIONS` (zero hits). The remaining 16 errors are all pre-existing: App.tsx StockItem mismatch ×2, KasirScreen warehouse-missing (WS4's deliberate lint signal), PurchaseOrderFormPage `key` prop, SalesInboxScreen `key` prop, Sidebar `'auth'` dead comparison, send-admin-invite Deno imports ×7. None of my edits added or removed an error message — the count delta is within noise tolerance for the harness's diff output.
- **Tests — 3/3 new pass, full `internal/db` regression green in 88.3s**: `go test ./internal/db/ -run 'TestAdminUsers_' -v` → 4 PASS (the three new tests + a pre-existing `TestAdminUsers_BackfillPermissions` that also stays green). Full regression `go test ./internal/db/` → `ok ... 88.303s` — every Phase 1 + Phase 2 T1-T11 test still green. The TDD path was clean: pre-migration run of `TestAdminUsers_PinColumnsExist` produced `missing column admin_users.approval_pin_hash` (expected RED); post-migration the same test passed first try. `TestAdminUsers_PgcryptoAvailable` was already GREEN before the migration because pgcrypto was already enabled on this DB (likely from a Supabase default or an earlier Phase 1 migration that needed it for some other purpose) — the `IF NOT EXISTS` clause makes my migration idempotent against that prior state.
- **Migration apply via psql (`supabase` CLI not on PATH)**: `CONN=$(grep ^SUPABASE_DB_CONNECTION backend-go/.env | sed 's/^SUPABASE_DB_CONNECTION=//') && /opt/homebrew/Cellar/libpq/18.4/bin/psql "$CONN" -f supabase/migrations/20260607000018_extend_permissions_and_pin.sql` — same recipe as T9/T10/T11. Output: `CREATE EXTENSION` (with a `NOTICE: extension "pgcrypto" already exists, skipping` — harmless, expected), `ALTER TABLE`, `UPDATE 4` (Owner rows), `UPDATE 1` (Staff Admin Toko or Staff Admin — only one matched), `UPDATE 0` (no Supervisor Gudang rows in this DB), `UPDATE 0` (no Finance Manager rows). Zero-row UPDATEs are correct given the DB's current admin_users population; the migration is forward-compatible — when new rows in those roles are inserted, they'll need to either run a one-shot per-row merge or have their `permissions` JSONB seeded by the User Management create form (which reads from `ALL_PERMISSIONS`).
- **What was NOT done (deliberate)**: did NOT add `verify_owner_pin` RPC or PIN lockout logic — that's T13's scope. Did NOT add a CHECK constraint on `pin_failed_count` (e.g., `>= 0`) — the column has a default 0 and is only mutated by T13's RPC, which can enforce the invariant. Did NOT seed `approval_pin_hash` for any user — Owners set their PIN via a dedicated User Management action (not in this task). Did NOT add an index on `pin_locked_until` — lockout check is a single-row lookup by id (no scan), no index needed. Did NOT modify the User Management screen to render the new "Akses Aksi" section — that's a frontend task downstream. Did NOT migrate existing admins to set `pin_failed_count = 0` explicitly via the migration — the column DEFAULT 0 covers new rows + the `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS … NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` backfills the column on existing rows automatically. Did NOT touch the other modified-but-uncommitted working-tree files (`.gitignore`, `backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `src/components/pembelian/MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, untracked plan/spec files, `.claire/`, `docs/haloai-demo/`, `docs/mekari-demo/`) — pre-existing user work, explicitly excluded per the bundled-named-files-only rule.
- **Self-review checklist**: (a) Migration filename `…018` matches the brief (plan body's `…011` is taken). (b) `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto` runs first. (c) Three PIN columns added with `IF NOT EXISTS` for idempotency. (d) Owner permissions JSONB merged with all 19 action keys true. (e) TypeScript `PermissionSet` extended with the same 19 keys as optional. (f) `ALL_PERMISSIONS` const includes the 19 new keys all set true. (g) 3 Go tests pass, full regression green. (h) TS typecheck baseline preserved (16 errors, none new from my changes). (i) Single commit, named files only.
- **Concerns**: ONE small concern — the migration's `UPDATE` statements have no effect on `Supervisor Gudang` or `Finance Manager` rows in this DB (`UPDATE 0` × 2 at apply time). Means any operator creating a Supervisor Gudang or Finance Manager admin user *after* this migration must either (a) re-run the same `||` merge UPDATE for that role, or (b) rely on the User Management create form's `ALL_PERMISSIONS` default (which grants ALL keys true — likely over-broad for non-Owner roles). Mitigation: the User Management create form should be updated downstream to apply role-specific defaults (not `ALL_PERMISSIONS`) for non-Owner roles — but that's a frontend task. For now, operators creating these roles manually need to know the action-key gap. Surfacing here so T13's author and the User Management refactor downstream see it.
- **Files**: `supabase/migrations/20260607000018_extend_permissions_and_pin.sql` (new, ~95 lines), `backend-go/internal/db/approvals_test.go` (+136 lines, 3 new tests appended), `src/types.ts` (+19 optional keys in `PermissionSet` + 19 true keys in `ALL_PERMISSIONS`), `progress.md` (this entry).
- **Commit**: `feat(approvals): extend admin_users.permissions with action keys + add Owner PIN columns` (SHA below).
- **Next**: Task 13 of Phase 2 — `verify_owner_pin` RPC (bcrypt compare + per-Owner lockout counter increment + auto-decide the approval_request on success). ## 2026-06-08 — Rakit Workflow, Task 0.2: RPCs migration (verbatim) — DONE_WITH_CONCERNS
- **Goal**: Phase 0 / Task 0.2 of sub-project B (Rakit Workflow). Land the second migration in the workflow series — the seven SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql RPCs that drive the rakit state machine (WIP → PENDING_LOCK_APPROVAL → AWAITING_LUNAS/PAID, with reject/withdraw/cancel/material-edit branches), plus the `_rakit_audit` helper that appends to `rakit_audit_log`. Plan instruction was explicit: write the SQL verbatim from the plan body, do NOT apply to live DB, syntactic check only, surface dependency mismatches as concerns rather than silently adapting. Slot `…009` (was `…002` in the plan but taken; `…008` was Task 0.1's schema migration committed at `fcb1dcc`).
- **What**: New file `supabase/migrations/20260608000009_rakit_workflow_rpcs.sql` (391 lines). Eight DDL objects: `_rakit_audit(...)` helper (audit-log insert), `submit_rakit_lock(p_transaction_id, p_lines, p_actor_id, p_actor_role)` (WIP → PENDING_LOCK_APPROVAL, upserts rakit_components from JSONB lines payload), `withdraw_rakit_lock(...)` (PENDING_LOCK_APPROVAL → WIP, clears lock_submitted_*), `reject_rakit_lock(p_reason, ...)` (PENDING_LOCK_APPROVAL → WIP with rejected-reason persisted), `approve_rakit_lock(p_hpp_overrides, ...)` (PENDING_LOCK_APPROVAL → AWAITING_LUNAS or PAID depending on `total_amount - dp_amount`; for detail-mode lines emits a stock_adjustments header + stock_adjustment_lines rows + per-component `_log_stock_movement` calls + direct `stocks.stock_atas/stock_bawah` decrements; for lumpsum-mode lines just stamps `hpp_final` from the lump sum or owner override), `cancel_rakit(p_refund_amount, p_reason, ...)` (WIP → CANCELLED with refund/forfeit math `forfeit = dp - refund`, bounds-checked `0 ≤ refund ≤ dp`), `material_edit_rakit(p_lines, ...)` (AWAITING_LUNAS → PENDING_LOCK_APPROVAL — reverses the original stock_adjustment via `_log_stock_movement` with negated qty_delta, stamps `reversed_at/reversed_by` on the old adjustment, clears `stock_adjustment_id` on the line, replaces components from the new JSONB lines payload, and resubmits for approval). Trailing `ALTER TABLE public.stock_adjustments ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS reversed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, reversed_by UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id);` to support the material-edit reversal flow.
- **Why verbatim and not adapted**: orientation revealed FOUR concrete mismatches between the plan's SQL and the Phase 1 stock-fraud / pre-existing schema. The plan's Step 3 anticipates dependency gaps and explicitly directs me to report them via DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, not to redesign. Adapting the call signatures or table schemas would be a design decision outside this task's delegation — the user (who authored both the plan AND Phase 1) needs to see the divergence surfaced so they can decide whether to revise the plan, evolve the Phase 1 schema, or add the missing `stock_adjustment_lines` table. Rewriting silently would bury that decision.
- **CONCERN 1 — `_log_stock_movement` signature mismatch (BLOCKING for runtime)**: actual function signature (`supabase/migrations/20260607000001b_log_stock_movement.sql`) is `(p_sku TEXT, p_warehouse TEXT, p_qty_delta INT, p_qty_before INT, p_source public.stock_movement_source, p_related_doc_type TEXT, p_related_doc_id TEXT, p_reason_code TEXT, p_reason_note TEXT, p_actor_user_id UUID, p_actor_role TEXT, p_evidence_urls TEXT[])`. The plan's call sites in `approve_rakit_lock` and `material_edit_rakit` use `p_movement_type` (should be `p_source`), `p_reference_type` (should be `p_related_doc_type`), `p_reference_id` (should be `p_related_doc_id`), `p_unit_cost` (no such parameter — does not exist on the helper), and **omit `p_qty_before` entirely** (no default — function will raise at runtime). Both call sites are broken as written.
- **CONCERN 2 — `stock_adjustments` schema mismatch (BLOCKING for runtime)**: actual schema (`supabase/migrations/20260607000008_stock_adjustments.sql`) is a single-row-per-adjustment approval-flow table: `(id BIGSERIAL, sku TEXT NOT NULL, warehouse TEXT NOT NULL, qty_delta INTEGER NOT NULL, reason_code stock_adjustment_reason NOT NULL, reason_note TEXT, evidence_urls TEXT[], requested_by UUID NOT NULL, requested_at TIMESTAMPTZ, approval_request_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES approval_requests(id), status TEXT, committed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, committed_movement_id BIGINT)`. The plan's INSERT in `approve_rakit_lock` targets columns `(adjustment_type, reason, reference_type, reference_id, approved_by, approved_at, created_by)` — NONE of which exist. Additionally `approval_request_id` is NOT NULL with no default, so the INSERT cannot succeed even with a column rename — the rakit-approval path does not flow through `approval_requests` (it's a direct Owner approval, not the staff-request → owner-approve loop).
- **CONCERN 3 — `stock_adjustment_lines` table does not exist (BLOCKING for runtime)**: `grep -rn "stock_adjustment_lines" supabase/migrations/` returns zero matches. The plan's `INSERT INTO public.stock_adjustment_lines (adjustment_id, sku, qty_delta, warehouse, fifo_cost)` in `approve_rakit_lock` and the `SELECT ... FROM stock_adjustment_lines` loop in `material_edit_rakit` both target a table that has never been created. The plan presupposes a header+lines normalisation that the Phase 1 design did not adopt (Phase 1 used a flat single-row table because approvals there are single-SKU). The rakit usage flow needs many SKUs per adjustment, which is why the plan introduces lines — but the lines table is referenced, not created. Either Phase 1 needs a follow-up migration to introduce `stock_adjustment_lines`, or the rakit RPCs need to redesign around the flat schema (one stock_adjustments row per component), or a parallel `rakit_stock_usage` table needs to be designed for this workflow.
- **CONCERN 4 — direct `UPDATE public.stocks SET stock_atas/stock_bawah` may be blocked by Phase 2 REVOKE**: `supabase/migrations/20260607000017_revoke_stocks_writes.sql` revoked UPDATE on `stocks` from anon/authenticated and re-granted only `(name, category, status, stock, specs, updated_at)`. SECURITY DEFINER means these RPCs run as the function owner (postgres), which retains the privilege — so this is NOT actually blocking. Mentioning it as a softer concern: if the user ever moves these RPCs to `SECURITY INVOKER` or runs ad-hoc fix-ups via the SDK, the direct stock decrements would fail. The canonical path going forward should probably be wrapping the qty mutation in `decrement_stock` or `_log_stock_movement` together — but that's a Phase 1 design question, not a Task 0.2 fix.
- **Syntactic verification (Step 2)**: counted via `grep` — 14 `$$` delimiters = 7 pairs = 7 function bodies, matches 7 `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`; 7 `BEGIN` paired with 7 `END $$;`; 7 `FOR ... LOOP` paired with 7 `END LOOP;`; 13 `IF`/`ELSIF` paired with 13 `END IF;`; parens balanced 87 open / 87 close. No unbalanced quotes (single quotes only inside string literals, no `''` continuations across line boundaries). Plpgsql structure is well-formed — file would parse cleanly through `psql --no-execute` even though runtime would fail on the three signature/schema mismatches above. Step 2's stated bar ("paren/quote balance, basic plpgsql structure") is met.
- **Dependency status snapshot (Step 3)**:
  - `public._log_stock_movement` — EXISTS (`20260607000001b_log_stock_movement.sql`, committed). Signature does NOT match plan's call sites (see CONCERN 1).
  - `public.stock_adjustments` — EXISTS (`20260607000008_stock_adjustments.sql`, committed). Schema does NOT match plan's INSERT (see CONCERN 2).
  - `public.stock_adjustment_lines` — DOES NOT EXIST anywhere in migrations (see CONCERN 3).
  - `public.stocks.stock_atas` / `stock_bawah` — EXIST (`20260605000002_warehouse_columns.sql`, committed).
  - Task 0.1 schema migration (`20260608000008_rakit_workflow_schema.sql`, commit `fcb1dcc`) — applied prior; `rakit_job_lines`, `rakit_components`, `rakit_audit_log`, `kasir_transactions.{lock_*, cancel_*, status='WIP'|'PENDING_LOCK_APPROVAL'}` all available.
- **What was NOT done (deliberate)**: did NOT apply the migration to any database — the task brief was explicit "user applies via their normal workflow". Did NOT adapt the plan's SQL to match the actual `_log_stock_movement` signature or `stock_adjustments` schema — per Step 3 + advisor guidance, dependency mismatches are surfaced as concerns, not silently fixed. Did NOT create a `stock_adjustment_lines` table to make the RPCs runnable — same rationale; the user needs to design that table (column types, FKs, RLS, indexes) before it can be added. Did NOT touch any of the modified-but-uncommitted working-tree files (`.gitignore`, `backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, `approvals_test.go`, `PembelianScreen.tsx`, untracked plan/spec/docs files) — pre-existing user work, out of scope for this task's commit.
- **Self-review checklist**: (a) File exists at `supabase/migrations/20260608000009_rakit_workflow_rpcs.sql`, 391 lines, slot `…009` is free (verified via `ls 20260608000009*` pre-write). (b) All 6 RPCs + `_rakit_audit` helper present and structurally valid — 7×`CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`, 7×`BEGIN`/`END $$`, parens 87/87, all `IF`/`LOOP` balanced. (c) Dependency audit done: 4 of 5 satisfied, 1 (`stock_adjustment_lines`) missing entirely + 2 (`_log_stock_movement` signature, `stock_adjustments` columns) mismatched — surfaced as CONCERNS 1-3 above. (d) Migration text matches plan body byte-for-byte modulo the filename comment header. (e) Single commit, only the new migration file + this progress entry in the diff.
- **Files**: `supabase/migrations/20260608000009_rakit_workflow_rpcs.sql` (new, 391 lines), `progress.md` (this entry).
- **Commit**: `feat(migration): rakit workflow RPCs — submit/approve/reject/cancel/withdraw/material-edit` (SHA below).
- **Next**: Before this migration can be applied to a live DB, the user needs to resolve Concerns 1-3 — either by patching the RPC SQL to match the actual `_log_stock_movement` signature + the existing `stock_adjustments` shape (or designing a new flat-vs-header decision), and by creating a `stock_adjustment_lines` table (or refactoring the rakit usage flow to fit the flat schema). Task 0.3 (Go integration test) will hit these same mismatches at first `db.Exec(seed_apply_migration)`, so it's the natural forcing function for the fix.

- **Goal**: Close the loop opened by WS3 — wire the cashier's warehouse selection (the existing `warehouse` state in `KasirScreen`, `'atas' | 'bawah'`, already used by the paid-now sale flow via `decrementStock`) through to `orderService.createWalkinDraft` so the WS3-required input field is satisfied. ## 2026-06-08 — Walk-in Stock Decrement, Task WS3: Types + service signature (warehouse) — DONE
- **Goal**: Plumb the `warehouse` selector from WS1's DB column into the TypeScript layer so WS4 can pass it from the KasirScreen UI. Two surgical edits: extend `DbOrder` with the optional `warehouse` field that mirrors the new DB column, and add `warehouse` as a required input to `orderService.createWalkinDraft` so every new walk-in draft is forced to declare which warehouse it's drawing from. The DB column is nullable (legacy whatsapp rows + pre-migration walkins) but the create-path is the choke point that should always know, so the input type is strict — `'atas' | 'bawah'`, no null/undefined.
- **What — `src/types.ts`**: One-line insertion in `DbOrder` immediately after `sales_channel: 'whatsapp' | 'walkin';` (around line 169 post-edit): `warehouse?: 'atas' | 'bawah' | null;`. Optional with explicit `| null` because the DB column allows NULL — historical rows from before WS1's `_006_orders_warehouse.sql` migration and all WhatsApp-channel orders will have it unset. WS4's payload type tightens it to required-non-null on the create path only.
- **What — `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts createWalkinDraft`**: Two edits to the same function (around lines 326-359). (1) Added `warehouse: 'atas' | 'bawah';` as the 5th field in the input type, placed after `customer_company` per the WS3 brief — required, no null, no undefined; the caller always knows. (2) Added `warehouse: input.warehouse,` to the `.insert(...)` payload immediately after `status` and before `customer_id`, matching the column order in WS1's migration. Resulting function signature is the same shape as before plus one field — preserves the `Promise<DbOrder>` return type and the existing `.select().single()` + cast-to-DbOrder return statement.
- **Why optional on `DbOrder` but required on the create input**: split-policy by direction. Reads come from rows of every vintage — pre-WS1, post-WS1, whatsapp-channel — so the type must permit `undefined` (column missing on legacy read) and `null` (column present but unset). Writes flow through `createWalkinDraft` only at this point, and the caller (`KasirScreen.handleSaveDraft` in WS4) will always know which warehouse the cashier picked. Making the input required forces a compile-time error if a new call-site forgets to pass it — which is exactly what lint now flags as the WS4 todo. ## 2026-06-08 — PO Create Page, Task 8: `PurchaseOrderFormPage` orchestrator — DONE_WITH_CONCERNS
- **Goal**: Fifth and culminating component of the PO Create page plan (after Tasks 4-7's sub-components). The full-page Create/Edit form that composes SupplierPicker + InlineSupplierForm + StockPicker + ItemRow into a single orchestrated experience. Replaces the modal-based `PurchaseOrderModal` flow with a dedicated sub-page rendered inside `PembelianScreen` (wiring in Task 9). Handles both creation (`po` prop undefined) and editing (`po` prop defined) — same component, mode-switched at the call site. Self-contained: owns all form state, validation, permission gating, dirty-tracking with confirm-on-back, and the actual `purchaseOrderService.create`/`.update`/`.markOrdered` calls.
- **What**: New file `src/components/pembelian/PurchaseOrderFormPage.tsx` (367 lines, single default-export functional component). 10-prop interface: `po?` (mode toggle), `suppliers/orders/stockList` (lookup data), `currentUserId/currentUserPermissions` (auth+RBAC), `onBack/onSaved/onSupplierAdded/showToast` (parent callbacks). Internal state: 9 `useState` hooks covering `supplierId`, `expectedReceiveDate`, `notes`, `taxEnabled/taxRate`, `items[]` (PoItemDraft[]), `showInlineSupplier/inlineSupplierPrefill` (inline supplier-create modal-within-form), `isDirty`, `saving`. Computed: `subtotal = sum(items.subtotal)`, `taxAmount = subtotal * taxRate%` when enabled, `total = subtotal + taxAmount`, plus `selectedSupplier` lookup. Layout: 4 vertical sections (sub-page header with Back + dirty pill, Detail PO with 12-col grid for Supplier/ExpectedDate/Notes, Items section with embedded StockPicker in the header + 12-col table of ItemRows, Ringkasan Biaya with right-aligned totals card) plus a sticky bottom footer with Simpan Draft + Simpan & Pesan buttons. Indonesian copy throughout, matching the Pembelian module's voice.
- **Why a single orchestrator over a split Detail/Items/Totals tri-page**: the plan spec says one page with three sections, and that matches the actual user flow — picking a supplier, adding items, and reviewing totals is one cognitive task ("write the PO"), not three. Tabs or wizard steps would force the user to click between sections to verify the items match the supplier's typical catalog, or to recalculate the total after a price tweak. A single scrollable page with sticky footer keeps total + actions always visible.
- **`canAct` permission gate via `useEffect` redirect — not a render guard**: when permissions deny, the page redirects via `onBack()` rather than rendering a "no access" panel. Rationale: this page is reached only via an explicit "Buat PO" / "Edit PO" CTA in `PembelianScreen` (Task 9). If a user without `can_create_po` somehow lands here (deep link, browser back-button, bookmark), bouncing them back to the list with a toast is better UX than freezing them on a dead-end page. The toast tells them why, the redirect tells them where to be. The check uses `!== false` (not `=== true`) so undefined permissions (e.g., legacy users with no permission row yet) default to ALLOW — matches the codebase convention (see `ALL_PERMISSIONS` in `types.ts`). This is permissive-by-default; the plan author chose this trade-off knowing the backend RLS will still enforce the actual write.
- **Dirty-tracking via `markDirty()` — opt-in per change, not effect-driven**: every state setter that mutates form data also calls `markDirty()`. The alternative (a `useEffect([supplierId, items, notes, ...])` that flips `isDirty` to true) would also fire on the INITIAL mount when the edit-mode setters seed from `po?.*` — false positive. Manual `markDirty()` on each handler is verbose but correct: only user-driven changes flip the dirty bit. `handleBack()` reads `isDirty` and shows `confirm('Perubahan belum disimpan...')` before letting the parent navigate away. The dirty pill in the header gives constant visual feedback.
- **Tax stored as fraction (0.11) but UI shows percent (11)**: the DB column is a fraction (existing convention from `PurchaseOrderModal`), so save-time we divide by 100 (`parseFloat(taxRate) / 100`). On load, multiply by 100 (`(po.tax_rate ?? 0) * 100`). Default 11% (Indonesian PPN). The `taxEnabled` checkbox is inferred from `(po.tax_rate ?? 0) > 0` — if the saved PO has tax_rate 0, the checkbox starts unchecked. Edge: a saved PO with exactly 0% explicit tax would lose the "user enabled tax" intent on reload, but since 0% tax is the same as no tax, this is fine.
- **`expected_receive_date` past-date warning, not block**: when the user picks a past date, the input border turns amber and a small "Tanggal sudah lewat. Boleh disimpan, jadi acuan delay." caption appears. Save still works. Rationale: editing an existing PO where the expected date has already passed (waiting for late delivery) is the EXACT use case — blocking it would defeat the purpose of the field. Future date or today's date → emerald border (success-ish). Empty → neutral gray. Three visual states wired via a ternary on `isPastDate(expectedReceiveDate)`. `isPastDate` compares ISO date strings lexicographically (safe for `YYYY-MM-DD` format), no Date object overhead.
- **Inline supplier create — modal-within-form via state toggle**: when the user types a supplier name with no match in SupplierPicker and clicks "Buat baru", SupplierPicker fires `onCreateNew(prefilledName)` which sets `inlineSupplierPrefill` + flips `showInlineSupplier=true`. The Supplier column in the Detail PO section then conditionally renders `<InlineSupplierForm>` instead of `<SupplierPicker>` — same slot, swapped UI. On success, `handleSupplierInlineSaved` selects the new supplier ID, hides the inline form, fires `onSupplierAdded()` to bubble up so `PembelianScreen` (Task 9) can refetch the supplier list, then marks dirty. Clean state machine, no nested modals.
- **Duplicate-SKU check on `handleAddItem` — toast + skip, not merge-qty**: Task 7's progress note flagged this as a Task 8 decision. The plan code (verbatim) chose toast-and-skip: if the user picks the same stock twice, they see `"Produk SKU-XXX sudah ada di list. Update qty-nya."` and the existing row is untouched. Rationale: silent qty-merge would be confusing when the user picks twice by accident (item disappears from search, qty quietly bumps from 1 to 2 — easy to miss); explicit toast tells them what to do. Trade-off: requires a manual scroll-down + qty edit instead of a one-click "+1". For the bulk-add flow this is fine; for power users this is friction. Future patch could add a "Tambah ke qty" CTA in the toast if friction emerges.
- **`payload.subtotal/tax_amount/total` sent to service — duplicates server-side compute**: the API contract still expects these as inputs (see `pembelianService.create`'s signature). We send them. The server is free to recompute and override for safety; we don't depend on our values surviving. This is defense-in-depth, not a contract change. The actual values come from our local computed `subtotal/taxAmount/total`, which are the same formulas the server uses — they should match.
- **`status` only set on CREATE, not on UPDATE**: in edit mode, `purchaseOrderService.update` receives the payload WITHOUT a `status` field (since `status` is controlled by separate state-machine RPCs like `markOrdered`). After update, if the user clicked "Simpan & Pesan" AND the PO was previously DRAFT, we additionally call `purchaseOrderService.markOrdered(po.id)` to flip it. If the PO is already ORDERED or beyond, the second call is skipped. Edge case: user edits a RECEIVED PO and clicks "Simpan & Pesan" — the update goes through but the `markOrdered` is skipped (correct, can't go backwards). The button label could arguably hide in this case; leaving it as the plan specified.
- **Sticky footer with `sticky bottom-0` — keeps actions in view when items list is long**: PO can have 30+ line items, scrolling makes the bottom buttons inaccessible without a long scroll-down. `sticky bottom-0 shadow-lg shadow-gray-200/40` keeps the action bar pinned, with a subtle top-shadow to visually separate from scrolled content. The total + item count are echoed in the footer so the user always sees what they're about to save. PDF-download caption appears only in edit-mode for non-DRAFT POs to nudge users toward the detail view for actual download (Task 11 wires the real download button in PoDetailView, not here).
- **`selectedSupplier` unused — kept anyway**: the task brief explicitly flagged this: `const selectedSupplier = suppliers.find(s => s.id === supplierId)` is computed but never read in the JSX (SupplierPicker handles its own selected-display via `selectedSupplierId` prop). Could be a "declared but never used" lint warning in stricter TS configs, but this repo's `tsconfig.app.json` doesn't enable `noUnusedLocals`. Verified: zero lint warning for this variable. Kept in case a future patch wants to render supplier metadata (phone, address) somewhere on this page — small forward-compat hook with zero cost today.
- **Lint verification — ONE new error, structurally identical to a pre-existing accepted pattern**: `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) → 12 errors total, of which 11 are pre-existing (App.tsx StockItem mismatch x2, SalesInboxScreen.tsx `key` prop on ChatBubbleProps x1, Sidebar.tsx `'auth'` dead comparison, send-admin-invite Deno imports x7). The NEW error is on line 284 of PurchaseOrderFormPage.tsx: `Property 'key' does not exist on type 'ItemRowProps'`. This is the SAME error pattern as the pre-existing `SalesInboxScreen.tsx:271` (`<ChatBubble key={msg.id} msg={msg} />`) which has been in the codebase since before this plan started. React reserves `key` as a special prop and TS technically should exempt it via the JSX intrinsic types, but with components that have a non-`HTMLAttributes`-extending props interface, TS strict mode flags it. The plan provided this code verbatim and the spec says "The file as written should compile clean against existing types" — so the plan author either was unaware of the SalesInboxScreen precedent error or considered the same-pattern duplication acceptable. I implemented the spec literally rather than diverging (e.g., extending `ItemRowProps` with `HTMLAttributes` or wrapping the map in a Fragment). Surfacing this as the primary "concern" for Task 9's author to triage.
- **What was NOT done (deliberate)**: did NOT wire this page into `PembelianScreen` — that's Task 9's integration step. Did NOT add the PDF download button — Task 11 does it on PoDetailView (the orchestrator just shows a hint caption when in edit mode + non-DRAFT). Did NOT add keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+S to save, Esc to back) — out of scope. Did NOT touch `PurchaseOrderModal.tsx` — the modal is being retired by Task 9 but is still wired up until then; killing it now would break the running app. Did NOT fix the `key` lint error (see above; intentional adherence to the plan spec). Did NOT touch the other modified-but-uncommitted working-tree files (`.gitignore`, `backend-go/daemon.pid`, `cloudbuild.frontend.yaml`, `MarkAsPaidModal.tsx`, untracked plan/specs files) — pre-existing user work, excluded per the task brief.
- **Self-review checklist**: (a) File path is exactly `src/components/pembelian/PurchaseOrderFormPage.tsx`. (b) Component signature matches the spec verbatim — 10 props, default-export functional component. (c) Permission gate via `useEffect` redirect with toast — correct for deep-link/bookmark scenarios. (d) `markDirty()` called inside every state-mutating handler — manual but correct. (e) Tax stored as fraction, displayed as percent — round-trips cleanly via `* 100` on load and `/ 100` on save. (f) `expected_receive_date` past-date warning is non-blocking — correct for late-delivery edit flows. (g) Inline supplier create slot-swaps within the Supplier column — clean state machine. (h) Duplicate SKU yields a toast + skip — matches the plan, leaves room for future "Tambah ke qty" affordance. (i) Status only set on CREATE; UPDATE uses separate `markOrdered` for DRAFT→ORDERED. (j) Sticky footer with shadow keeps actions visible on long item lists. (k) ONE new lint error (`key` prop on ItemRow), structurally identical to pre-existing `SalesInboxScreen.tsx:271` — surfaced as a concern, not silently bypassed. (l) Single clean commit, only the new file in the diff.
- **Concerns**: ONE primary concern — the new lint error on line 284 (`key` prop not on ItemRowProps). Mitigation options for Task 9 author: (i) extend `ItemRowProps extends React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` in ItemRow.tsx (minimal-touch, idiomatic React), or (ii) extract the loop into a sub-component that accepts and consumes the key correctly, or (iii) accept the warning as consistent with the SalesInboxScreen.tsx precedent. Recommendation: do (i) when touching ItemRow.tsx next, since it's a one-line type fix that solves both the new error AND the precedent.
